FearoftheUnknownStart.4.full: It is with great reticence that I relay a grievous event which occurred upon my arrival. It is my hope that in penning these thoughts my mind will find solace from the foul images that have so firmly embedded themselves.
FearoftheUnknownStart.4.easy: I do not want to write this, but I must tell you about a terrible thing that happened when I arrived. I hope that writing it down will calm my mind and free me from the ugly pictures that I cannot forget.
FearoftheUnknownStart.4.short: I must, reluctantly, relate a terrible event from my arrival, in the hope that writing it will bring my mind some peace.

FearoftheUnknownStart.5.full: I will spare you the details of the journey to that dismal village to settle my deceased father's affairs. But upon entering its unpaved limits, my spouse drew my attention to several men and women galloping towards the town center, where there was a loud commotion and gathering of individuals. Intrigued by the local pageantry, I resolved to indulge my curiosity. I rapped my knuckles against the roof of the carriage and asked for the driver to turn towards the festivities.
FearoftheUnknownStart.5.easy: I will not tell you about the long trip to that sad village, where I went to take care of my dead father's business. But when we came into the village, on its dirt roads, my spouse showed me several men and women riding fast towards the town center. There was a lot of noise there, and many people had come together. I thought it was a local festival and I wanted to see it. I knocked on the roof of the carriage and asked the driver to go towards the celebration.
FearoftheUnknownStart.5.short: Arriving to settle my late father's affairs, we saw villagers galloping toward a commotion in the town center. Curious, I told the driver to turn towards it.

FearoftheUnknownStart.6.full: He did not respond to my insistence. Nor did he respond when I thrice repeated my command. Frustrated, I angled my head out of the carriage window in order to speak more firmly. That is when I spied the horrific source of his obstinate and wise decision. For the briefest of moments — though a moment long enough for it to be etched within my memory forever — I saw the source of the commotion: A crowd of people surrounded a tall wooden stage where, swinging slowly from a thick hemp noose, hung a youthful woman. Her lifeless eyes stared in my direction before her form was obscured by buildings.
FearoftheUnknownStart.6.easy: He did not answer me. He did not answer when I said it three more times. I was angry, so I put my head out of the carriage window to speak to him more strongly. That is when I saw why he had wisely refused. For a very short moment, but long enough that I will never forget it, I saw the reason for the noise: a crowd of people stood around a tall wooden stage. On it, a young woman was hanging from a thick rope around her neck, slowly turning. Her dead eyes looked at me, and then the buildings hid her from my view.
FearoftheUnknownStart.6.short: The driver ignored me. When I leaned out to insist, I saw why: a crowd around a tall wooden stage, where a young woman swung slowly from a noose. Her lifeless eyes met mine before the buildings hid her.

FearoftheUnknownStart.7.full: An irrational fear has gripped the populace. I swear it. The region is rife with superstitious traditions; traditions that do not mix well with the Church's rigid moral compass. When an individual from this close-knit community emerges from shuttered windows, they eye me as one would a foreigner, with sideways glances that make each excursion there insufferable. Accusations of witchcraft and voodooism erupt with increasing fervor, and paranoia weaves its tendrils into their minds.
FearoftheUnknownStart.7.easy: A fear without reason has taken hold of the people. I promise you, it is true. There are many old superstitions in this region, and they do not go well with the strict rules of the Church. When someone from this small, close community comes out from behind their closed windows, they look at me as if I were a stranger. Their looks from the side make every trip into the village terrible. People accuse each other of witchcraft and voodoo more and more often, and fear grows in their minds like a plant.
FearoftheUnknownStart.7.short: An irrational fear grips the people. Old superstitions clash with the Church, villagers eye me like a foreigner, and accusations of witchcraft spread as paranoia takes root.

FearoftheUnknownStart.8.full: Maybe this forced solitude will prove beneficial to my wits, as even amidst this clamor I find myself unnaturally focused. I have recently discovered my father's leather-bound journal and, while somewhat trite, I feel it has sparked something within me; a direction for my future studies, perhaps. Maybe it will offer some amusement in these trying times.
FearoftheUnknownStart.8.easy: Maybe being alone like this will be good for my mind, because even with all this noise, I can think very clearly. I have just found my father's journal, with its leather cover. It is a little boring, but I feel it has woken something inside me. Maybe it shows me what I should study in the future. Maybe it will at least entertain me in these difficult times.
FearoftheUnknownStart.8.short: Strangely, this solitude sharpens my focus. My father's leather-bound journal has sparked something in me: perhaps a direction for my studies.

S4Kill1.3.full: It is nearing midnight now, and I struggle to find my words. Is this remorse I feel, or elation? Even as I was swept into the midst of the frightened crowd, watching the flames swirl upwards, I was spellbound by their savagery. I could not imagine that this paranoia would be exercised so bluntly!
S4Kill1.3.easy: It is almost midnight now, and it is hard for me to find the right words. Do I feel sorry, or do I feel joy? Even as the frightened crowd pulled me along, and I watched the flames go up into the sky, I could not stop watching how wild they were. I never thought that people would act on their fear so openly!
S4Kill1.3.short: It is nearly midnight. Remorse or elation? Swept along by the crowd, I watched the flames rise, spellbound by their savagery.

S4Kill1.4.full: It began over supper with my siblings: **The Blacksmith** - accused of practicing witchcraft - was carried past our brasserie to the steps of Town Hall. He wailed and protested his innocence, and when allowed use of his hands, he immediately accused Henriette, the town **Butcher**, of beguiling him. Within moments, he dramatically convulsed and acted as if under a trance when she decried his accusation.
S4Kill1.4.easy: It started at dinner with my siblings: **The Blacksmith**, who was accused of witchcraft, was carried past our restaurant to the steps of Town Hall. He screamed and said he was innocent. When they let him use his hands, he quickly accused Henriette, the town **Butcher**, of putting a spell on him. When she said his accusation was false, he suddenly shook his whole body and acted as if he were under a spell.
S4Kill1.4.short: At supper with my siblings, we saw **The Blacksmith**, accused of witchcraft, dragged to Town Hall. He protested his innocence and accused Henriette, the town **Butcher**, of bewitching him, then put on a show of convulsions.

S4Kill1.5.full: As we investigated the commotion that had interrupted our dessert course more closely, the **Blacksmith's** eyes blazed with fiery determination. He pled with us specifically. He would offer us his services, whatever we needed to spare his life.
S4Kill1.5.easy: The noise had stopped our dessert, so we went to look more closely. The **Blacksmith's** eyes were burning with a strong will. He begged us directly. He would offer us his services, anything we needed, if we saved his life.
S4Kill1.5.short: When we went closer, the **Blacksmith** begged us directly: his services, whatever we needed, if we spared his life.

S4Kill1.6.full: The **Butcher** was pressed to the steps of Town Hall. Silent, innocent as she approached, and forlorn. We knew that Henriette would offer the same deal.
S4Kill1.6.easy: The **Butcher** was pushed to the steps of Town Hall. She came silently, innocent and very sad. We knew that Henriette would offer us the same deal.
S4Kill1.6.short: The silent, forlorn **Butcher** was pushed to the steps. We knew Henriette would offer the same deal.

S4Kill1.7.full: There was no way to slake the public's thirst for catharsis without bloodshed. Tonight, a witch was burned.
S4Kill1.7.easy: The people wanted to let out their feelings, and only blood could satisfy them. Tonight, a witch was burned.

S4Blacksmith.3.full: Though a ghastly event, it was perhaps fortunate. As the blaze extinguished and the crowd dispersed, no eyes cast their suspicious gaze upon myself, nor my cousins.
S4Blacksmith.3.easy: It was a terrible event, but maybe it was lucky for us. When the fire went out and the crowd left, nobody looked at me or my cousins with suspicion.
S4Blacksmith.3.short: Grim, but fortunate: when the fire died and the crowd left, no one suspected me or my cousins.

S4Blacksmith.4.full: Henriette was exceedingly appreciative of our vote of confidence and offered us a discount on her services. No questions asked.
S4Blacksmith.4.easy: Henriette was very thankful that we had supported her, and she offered us a lower price for her services. No questions asked.

S4Blacksmith.5.full: Each player who voted **NAY** quickly rummages through the Blacksmith's final offerings during the chaos and **gains 1 {icon:Gears_Icon}**.

S4Butcher.3.full: The Blacksmith laughed and shook each of our hands with a knowing wink. He will offer a deep discount on his services in the future. No questions asked.
S4Butcher.3.easy: The Blacksmith laughed and shook hands with each of us, with a wink that said he knew. In the future, he will offer his services to us at a much lower price. No questions asked.

S4Butcher.4.full: What an especially eventful dinner party. (Note to self - retrieve the recipe for the apricot glaze from tonight's menu.)
S4Butcher.4.easy: What an exciting dinner party. (Note to self: get the recipe for the apricot sauce from tonight's menu.)

S4Witch1.5.full: With your return from university imminent, I thought it best to relay to you the state of affairs in {0}.

S4Witch1.6.full: For a few years, I watched as the village's hostilities softened and the peasantry returned to their quaint ways of living. But, before long, old rumors of pagan worship and occult manipulations resurfaced. The village has become united in the opinion that the **public execution of the humble Butcher** was a false spectacle, and that insidious characters still lurk within the town limits.
S4Witch1.6.easy: For a few years, I watched the people of the village become less angry, and the farmers went back to their simple old ways. But soon the old stories about pagan religions and dark magic came back. Now the whole village believes that the **public execution of the humble Butcher** was a false show, and that dangerous people are still hiding in the town.
S4Witch1.6.short: The village calmed for a few years, but the old rumors of pagan worship returned. Now all agree the **public execution of the humble Butcher** was a sham, and that sinister people still lurk in town.

S4Witch1.7.full: Unfortunately, the town became further incensed and searched for an alternative solution.

S4Witch1.12.full: With your return from university imminent, I thought it best to relay to you the state of affairs in {0}.

S4Witch1.13.full: For a few years, I watched as the village's hostilities softened and the peasantry returned to their quaint ways of living. And as the years continued, the horrible spectacle of **the Blacksmith's execution** soon became a strictly taboo subject. Your scientific efforts and somewhat ignoble deeds were deemed eccentric. Each day, the townspeople grow more accepting of the exotic nature of the world.
S4Witch1.13.easy: For a few years, I watched the people of the village become less angry, and the farmers went back to their simple old ways. As the years went on, nobody was allowed to talk about the terrible show of **the Blacksmith's execution** anymore. People thought your scientific work and your not very honorable actions were just strange. Every day, the people of the town accept a little more that the world is full of unusual things.
S4Witch1.13.short: The village calmed, and **the Blacksmith's execution** became a taboo subject. Your science and questionable deeds were thought merely eccentric, and the townspeople grow more accepting of the world's strangeness.

S4Witch1.14.full: It is a curious thing to observe.

S4Witch2.5.full: You must forgive the lateness of my writing, but as your caretaker, I regret to say that I am not very acquainted with the quill. I have kept your affairs in order to the best of my ability, but I am troubled by recent events in {0}.
S4Witch2.5.easy: Please forgive me for writing so late. I take care of your house, and I am sorry to say that I do not write very well. I have looked after your business as well as I can, but I am worried about things that have happened in {0} recently.
S4Witch2.5.short: Forgive my late and clumsy letter. As your caretaker I have kept your affairs in order, but recent events in {0} trouble me.

S4Witch2.6.full: For a few years, I watched as the village's hostilities softened and the peasantry returned to their quaint ways of living. But, before long, old rumors of pagan worship and occult manipulations resurfaced.
S4Witch2.6.easy: For a few years, I watched the people of the village become less angry, and the farmers went back to their simple old ways. But soon the old stories about pagan religions and dark magic came back.
S4Witch2.6.short: The village calmed for a few years, but soon the old rumors of pagan worship and the occult returned.

S4Witch2.7.full: With **no one overtaken to slake the mob's thirst**, their intense fear of outsiders has surged into a frenzy.
S4Witch2.7.easy: With **no one taken to satisfy the angry crowd**, their strong fear of strangers has grown into madness.

S4Witch2.8.full: I fear their suspicions have increased. Please be safe in your return.

S4Witch2.13.full: You must forgive me for not responding sooner, but I must admit that there is not much to tell. While initially I suspected that the softening of the village's hostilities would be brief, indeed, old rumors of pagan worship and occult manipulations resurfaced in the coming years.
S4Witch2.13.easy: Please forgive me for not writing back sooner, but there is not much to tell. At first I thought the village would only stay calm for a short time. And it is true, the old stories about pagan religions and dark magic came back in the following years.
S4Witch2.13.short: Forgive my slow reply; there is little to tell. As I feared, the old rumors of pagan worship and the occult returned in the following years.

S4Witch2.14.full: However, these rumors were quelled by the boasts of townsfolk who had removed the evil blight on the land with torches and pitchforks. The **mob had been appeased** and the paranoia so entrenched within the village now appears a distant memory.
S4Witch2.14.easy: But these stories stopped because some townspeople proudly said that they had removed the evil from the land with torches and pitchforks. The **angry crowd had been calmed**, and the deep fear in the village now seems like something from long ago.
S4Witch2.14.short: But townsfolk boasted of driving out the evil with torches and pitchforks. The **mob had been appeased**, and the paranoia now seems a distant memory.

S4Witch2.15.full: There is no need to rush home, though we send you warm wishes all the same.

ForeignIntro.4.full: I hope you will forgive the direct manner in which this letter is received. Due to recent events, I no longer entrust my correspondence to postal carriers and prefer to hire discrete private couriers. This message is meant for your eyes only and I will not allow those who so blatantly scheme against me an opportunity to uncover my motives!
ForeignIntro.4.easy: Please forgive me for sending this letter in such an unusual way. Because of recent events, I no longer trust mail carriers with my letters. I prefer to pay private messengers who keep secrets. This message is only for you. I will not give the people who plan against me so openly a chance to find out what I want to do!
ForeignIntro.4.short: Forgive this direct delivery: after recent events I trust only discreet private couriers. This is for your eyes alone; I will not let those scheming against me learn my motives!

ForeignIntro.6.full: I have only just been situated these past few months with my spouse and close servants, and scarcely familiarized myself with the thatched-roofs and bucolic scenery, yet already I have seen the fires blaze at night, the screams of the damned, and the gibbet creaking under the weight of swinging bodies. The mob comes with torches in the evening and rips the accused from their residences. It appears that my parent's warnings proved true. The occult hysteria that they endured has returned in earnest! I fear that I may be next!
ForeignIntro.6.easy: I have only lived here for a few months with my spouse and my closest servants. I hardly know the houses with straw roofs and the country views yet. But I have already seen fires burning at night, heard the screams of the damned, and seen the gallows creak under the weight of hanging bodies. The angry crowd comes with torches in the evening and pulls the accused people out of their homes. It seems my parents' warnings were true. The fear of dark magic that they lived through has truly come back! I am afraid that I will be next!
ForeignIntro.6.short: Only months after settling here, I have seen fires at night, heard the screams, and watched the gibbet creak. The mob drags the accused from their homes. My parents' warnings were true: the occult hysteria has returned, and I fear I am next!

ForeignIntro.7.full: Even my own cousins have begun to eye me like mongrel dogs, yearning for scraps. In their jealous mania, they wish to uncover my secrets and claim them for their own. I can see how they desire to place the blame upon me; to distract me from completing my family's important scientific work! It would break my heart to see ill come to them, yet if they continue in their provocations, I will not hesitate to unleash the fires of hell upon them.
ForeignIntro.7.easy: Even my own cousins have started to look at me like hungry dogs waiting for scraps. In their jealous madness, they want to discover my secrets and take them for themselves. I can see that they want to blame me, to stop me from finishing my family's important scientific work! It would break my heart if something bad happened to them. But if they keep provoking me, I will not wait to send the fires of hell after them.
ForeignIntro.7.short: Even my jealous cousins eye me like hungry dogs, eager to steal my secrets and blame me, to keep me from my family's scientific work. If they keep provoking me, I will unleash the fires of hell upon them.

ForeignIntro.8.full: But I am secure in my ambitions. I have uncovered my true purpose. I will not succumb to fear. My secret work consumes my waking hours and I will stop at nothing to see it come to fruition!
ForeignIntro.8.easy: But I am sure of my plans. I have found my true purpose. I will not let fear win. My secret work takes all of my time when I am awake, and I will do anything to make it succeed!
ForeignIntro.8.short: But I have found my true purpose and will not succumb to fear. My secret work consumes me, and I will stop at nothing to complete it!

CreatureIntro.4.full: As mariners are wont to say; there is always a lull before the storm. As I am wont to say; a lowering of barometric pressure generally occurs before the storm. And this idiom certainly applies to the horror of my current situation.
CreatureIntro.4.easy: Sailors like to say that it is always calm before a storm. I like to say that the air pressure usually goes down before a storm. And this saying is very true for the horrible situation I am in now.
CreatureIntro.4.short: Sailors speak of a lull before the storm; I speak of falling barometric pressure. Either way, it fits my current horror.

CreatureIntro.5.full: My family's manor is set on a small precipice, its imposing iron gate emerging from the forest like the mouth of an otherworldly beast. You have no doubt seen the daguerreotype, so I will not delve further into detail. I remembered the daunting architecture from my youth, and returning to claim my inheritance left me feeling trepidatious.
CreatureIntro.5.easy: My family's house stands on a small cliff. Its big iron gate comes out of the forest like the mouth of a monster from another world. You have surely seen the photograph, so I will not describe it more. I remembered the frightening building from when I was young, and coming back to take my inheritance made me nervous.
CreatureIntro.5.short: My family's manor sits on a precipice, its iron gate rising from the forest like a beast's mouth. Returning to claim my inheritance, I felt uneasy.

CreatureIntro.6.full: Whatever the cause, it appears the delirium of the past has ebbed and conversations about the darker history of the town are now relegated to whispers in private. The consensus is that justice has been served and modern living has prevailed over the old ways. In fact, there are many who deny that the events occurred at all.
CreatureIntro.6.easy: Whatever the reason, the madness of the past seems to have gone away. People now only whisper in private about the dark history of the town. Most people believe that justice has been done and that modern life has won over the old ways. In fact, many people say that those events never happened at all.
CreatureIntro.6.short: The old delirium has ebbed; the town's dark history is only whispered about. Most believe justice was served and modern living has won. Many deny it happened at all.

CreatureIntro.7.full: The underlying symptoms of mass hysteria have channeled themselves into other menial and unproductive modes of thinking. I am of the opinion that they overcompensate for the shames of their past. While the ground has just been broken, the district has invested in the most modern alienist philosophies — absurd and untested as those theories are — and a new Asylum is being constructed to focus on the rehabilitation of the mind.
CreatureIntro.7.easy: The deep problem of mass fear has turned into other small and useless ways of thinking. I believe that people are trying too hard to make up for the shame of their past. Work has only just started, but the district has paid for the most modern ideas about curing the mind, even though those ideas are silly and nobody has tested them. A new Asylum is being built to help people heal their minds.
CreatureIntro.7.short: The mass hysteria now finds other outlets; I think the town overcompensates for its shameful past. The district has bought into modern, untested theories of the mind, and a new Asylum is being built for its rehabilitation.

CreatureIntro.8.full: So, like a wolf licking its wounds, the town has returned to a relative peace. And for a moment, it seemed that the calm would provide a welcome atmosphere to return to my labors.
CreatureIntro.8.easy: So, like a wolf that takes care of its wounds, the town is fairly peaceful again. And for a moment, it seemed that this calm would be a good time to go back to my work.
CreatureIntro.8.short: Like a wolf licking its wounds, the town is at peace again, and for a moment the calm seemed perfect for my work.

CreatureIntro.9.full: That is, until the Creature appeared in my window one night, it's bulky frame wet with rain.
CreatureIntro.9.easy: That was true until one night, when the Creature appeared at my window, its big body wet from the rain.

S4Jail2.3.full: Is it true they have plans to convert the Asylum into a private penitentiary? If I were to venture a guess, I would assume **your investments** may have had a hand in it.
S4Jail2.3.easy: Is it true that they plan to turn the Asylum into a private prison? If I had to guess, I would say that **your investments** helped make this happen.
S4Jail2.3.short: Is the Asylum to become a private penitentiary? I suspect **your investments** had a hand in it.

S4Jail2.4.full: Well, I say good riddance. The thought of spending precious resources to reform a mind already lost when they could be put to better use manually. It is like trying to unrotten a rotten fruit!
S4Jail2.4.easy: Well, I am happy to see it go. Why spend valuable money to fix a mind that is already lost, when those people could do useful work with their hands? It is like trying to make a rotten fruit fresh again!
S4Jail2.4.short: Good riddance. Why waste resources reforming lost minds that could be put to work? It is like trying to unrot a rotten fruit!

S4Jail2.5.full: Since your last letter, I have heard rumors that with **generous financial backing** from some anonymous donors, they are expanding the Asylum. Given your disposition, I would not be surprised to discover that you had a direct hand in it.
S4Jail2.5.easy: Since your last letter, I have heard that the Asylum is getting bigger, thanks to **a lot of money** from some unknown people. Knowing you, I would not be surprised to learn that you helped with this directly.
S4Jail2.5.short: I hear that, with **generous financial backing** from anonymous donors, the Asylum is expanding. I suspect your direct involvement.

S4Jail2.6.full: I say it is a positive thing, this mental rehabilitation. I've always been intrigued by the potential of the human mind both to adapt and to be adapted upon. Though, I suggest you keep your distance. They may mistake your jocularity for insanity and admit you. Wouldn't that be something?
S4Jail2.6.easy: I think it is a good thing, this healing of the mind. I have always found it interesting how the human mind can change, and how others can change it. But I think you should stay away from it. They might think your jokes are madness and lock you in. Wouldn't that be something?
S4Jail2.6.short: I welcome this rehabilitation; the mind's power to adapt, and be adapted, fascinates me. But keep your distance, lest they mistake your jokes for madness and admit you!

IsolationIntro.4.full: I tell you, these damn peasants actually built a wall around their own town. In the 1800's no less! These fools have traded paranoia for utter delusion!
IsolationIntro.4.easy: I tell you, these terrible farmers really built a wall around their own town. In the 1800s! These fools have stopped being afraid and have become completely crazy instead!
IsolationIntro.4.short: These peasants have built a wall around their own town. In the 1800s! They have traded paranoia for delusion!

IsolationIntro.5.full: Do they expect a foreign government to set up a military line and trebuchets to lay siege to this backwater stronghold? What on earth would it offer them? Trade has suffered. Prices have risen. And most importantly, with the caravans left to go elsewhere, I must find alternative ways to procure knowledge.
IsolationIntro.5.easy: Do they think a foreign government will send soldiers and war machines to attack this small, poor fortress? What could it possibly give them? Trade has become worse. Prices have gone up. And most importantly, now that the traders go to other places, I must find new ways to get knowledge.
IsolationIntro.5.short: Do they expect a foreign siege of this backwater? Trade has suffered and prices have risen, and with the caravans gone I must find other sources of knowledge.

IsolationIntro.6.full: Why just this week, I was enraged by the audacity of the intrusion into my affairs! I, the rightful heir to a considerable estate, was forced to suffer the indignity of a physical inspection at what appeared to be a freshly fashioned gateway to the village where I was born. And then, to infer that I was bound by duty to prove my citizenship? My spouse was so manhandled that they were forced to spend the next week in their bedroom consumed by anxious thoughts.
IsolationIntro.6.easy: Just this week, I was very angry because people dared to interfere in my business! I am the true heir to a large property, but I had to accept the shame of being searched at a new gate to the village where I was born. And then they said I had to prove that I am a citizen! They treated my spouse so roughly that they had to stay in their bedroom for the next week, full of worry.
IsolationIntro.6.short: This week I, the rightful heir to a considerable estate, was searched at a new gate to my own birthplace and told to prove my citizenship! My spouse was so manhandled they spent a week in bed with nerves.

IsolationIntro.7.full: Curse this infernal world filled with frustrations and complications at every turn! If only these regressive tendencies toward isolationism could have been resolved in another way! Surely, you can determine how dire the situation has become if it has rattled my notoriously pragmatic disposition. How can one change the world when it so decidedly wants to remain the same?
IsolationIntro.7.easy: I hate this world, full of problems and difficulties everywhere! If only this wish to close the town off from the world could have been solved in another way! You can surely see how bad things have become if even I, who am known for being so practical, am this upset. How can anyone change the world when the world so clearly wants to stay the same?
IsolationIntro.7.short: Curse this world of frustrations! If even I, notoriously pragmatic, am rattled, you see how dire it is. How can one change a world so determined to stay the same?

IsolationIntro.8.full: Mark my words, I would sooner watch these ramparts crumble than allow them to destroy my spirit. I will find a way to circumvent this oppressive state and preserve my legacy at all costs!
IsolationIntro.8.easy: Remember what I say: I would rather see these walls fall down than let them break my spirit. I will find a way around this cruel government and protect my family's work, whatever it costs!
IsolationIntro.8.short: I would sooner see these walls crumble than my spirit. I will find a way around them and preserve my legacy at all costs!

TensionIntro.4.full: Ah, what relief it is for one to not spend each waking moment fearing they will be burned at the stake! The oppressive hostilities of the Romanian countryside, of which I had become familiar during my youth, made the anxiety of my carriage-bound return to the old estate a dreadful prospect.
TensionIntro.4.easy: Oh, what a relief it is not to spend every moment afraid of being burned alive! When I was young, I came to know the cruel hate of the Romanian countryside. Because of this, I was very afraid of my return to the old house in a carriage.
TensionIntro.4.short: What relief not to fear being burned at the stake! Remembering the countryside's hostility from my youth, I had dreaded my return to the old estate.

TensionIntro.5.full: Yet, even as the ink dried upon the executor's paperwork, my spouse and I quietly enjoyed our coffee against the bustle of a cobblestone street. The only eyes upon us were those clearly impressed by our bright, Parisian attire. Never once did an errant gaze suggest I would be shot with a revolver or murdered viciously by a stiletto. It was almost disappointing.
TensionIntro.5.easy: But even while the ink was drying on the papers about my inheritance, my spouse and I quietly enjoyed our coffee on a busy stone street. The only people who looked at us were clearly impressed by our bright clothes from Paris. Not once did anyone look at me in a way that made me think I would be shot with a gun or killed cruelly with a knife. It was almost disappointing.
TensionIntro.5.short: Yet as the paperwork dried, my spouse and I enjoyed coffee on a bustling street, admired only for our Parisian attire. No one looked ready to shoot or stab me. It was almost disappointing.

TensionIntro.6.full: With the town's decision to forgo construction of a barrier, the emergence of additional trade and the ceasing of xenophobic hostilities has allowed further interaction with other cultures. I find myself entertaining exotic guests that pique my darker interests. The occult and its superstitious effects on my family's past has become a peculiar fascination. Spiritualism being the fashion these days, you know.
TensionIntro.6.easy: The town decided not to build a wall. Because of this, more trade has come, and the hate of strangers has stopped, so people can meet other cultures more. I now welcome unusual guests who wake my interest in dark things. Dark magic and the effect of superstition on my family's past have become a strange passion for me. Talking to the spirits of the dead is very popular these days, you know.
TensionIntro.6.short: Without a wall, trade has grown and the hostility toward outsiders has ended. I now entertain exotic guests who feed my fascination with the occult and my family's past. Spiritualism is the fashion, you know.

TensionIntro.7.full: However, "old habits die hard" as the saying goes, and a delicious tension roils beneath the surface of the town. Acceptance (or apathy) may have calmed the tempest of hatred, but I realize that this deep psychological infection has yet to be fully reconciled. With each visit, I feel my actions push these factions closer until they will be forced to make a potentially devastating and amusing decision.
TensionIntro.7.easy: But, as people say, "old habits die hard", and a wonderful tension is moving under the surface of the town. Acceptance, or maybe not caring, may have calmed the storm of hate. But I understand that this deep sickness of the mind is not completely healed. With every visit, I feel that my actions push these groups closer together, until they must make a decision that could be terrible, and fun to watch.
TensionIntro.7.short: But old habits die hard, and a delicious tension simmers beneath the town. The hatred has calmed, not healed. With each visit I push these factions closer to a devastating, and amusing, decision.

TensionIntro.8.full: It is an experiment in itself; a powder keg waiting to go off. And I am desperate to observe the results.
TensionIntro.8.easy: It is an experiment in itself, like a barrel of gunpowder that is about to explode. And I cannot wait to see what happens.

S4Asylum.2.full: The Asylum, while marginally effective in its treatments, appears to be struggling financially - something which I had cautioned earlier about the town's philanthropic pursuits. Lock a deranged person in a room and inevitably the cost of care will outweigh the revenue received.
S4Asylum.2.easy: The Asylum helps its patients a little, but it seems to have money problems. I had warned the town about this when they started their generous projects. If you lock a mad person in a room, the cost of caring for them will always be more than the money that comes in.
S4Asylum.2.short: The Asylum, only marginally effective, is struggling financially, as I had warned. Locking up the deranged always costs more than it earns.

S4Asylum.3.full: Of course, I was once again asked for assistance: "Surely you are familiar with Hanwell Asylum and the recent progressive reforms presented by Mattineau. Rehabilitation is the moral treatment option,” they repeated. I was glad that at least in this scenario, their fundraising efforts came with a tangible reward.
S4Asylum.3.easy: Of course, they asked me for help again: "Surely you know Hanwell Asylum and the new modern changes that Mattineau has suggested. Healing the patients is the right thing to do,” they said again and again. I was happy that this time, at least, giving them money came with a real reward.
S4Asylum.3.short: Naturally, they asked me for help again, citing Hanwell Asylum and Mattineau's reforms: "Rehabilitation is the moral option.” At least this time, their fundraising came with a real reward.

PrivatizedIntro.4.full: I will keep this letter brief — as brief as I can. You are aware that brevity is not my strongest suit. However, it is August, the ink struggles to dry in the humidity, and my mind is set on complicated things. Perhaps it would be more amiable to pen this missive in my own blood, cold as I am perceived to be by the inhabitants of this gray, lifeless city. It would certainly bring a little more color to it.
PrivatizedIntro.4.easy: I will keep this letter short, as short as I can. You know that I am not good at being brief. But it is August, the ink does not dry well in the wet air, and my mind is busy with difficult things. Maybe it would be nicer to write this letter in my own blood, as the people of this gray, dead city think I am so cold. It would certainly give the city a little more color.
PrivatizedIntro.4.short: I will try to be brief, never my strength. It is a humid August and my mind is on complicated things. Perhaps I should write in my own blood; it would add some color to this gray, lifeless city.

PrivatizedIntro.5.full: You are probably interested in matters of business, and it is going exceedingly well, or so I hear — I struggle to keep the figures in my head. I, and regrettably my good cousins, whom I love dearly, have invested directly in the town's well-being and now own a substantial portion of the commercial district. It appears that my parent's investments have paid off handsomely.
PrivatizedIntro.5.easy: You are probably interested in business, and it is going very well, or so people tell me. It is hard for me to remember the numbers. I, and also my good cousins, whom I love very much, have put money directly into the town, and now we own a large part of the shopping district. It seems that my parents' investments have earned a lot of money.
PrivatizedIntro.5.short: Business is excellent, I hear; I cannot keep the figures in my head. My cousins and I have invested directly in the town and now own much of the commercial district. My parents' investments have paid off handsomely.

PrivatizedIntro.6.full: News of the day: The Asylum Project, which I believe was misguided from the beginning, has become a more intriguing source of labor. It's not that I believe that rehabilitation of the deviant mindset is impossible, it simply requires a more aggressive therapy than they were willing to indulge. With our unmediated assistance and the endorsement of the state, a prison is a more versatile testing ground.
PrivatizedIntro.6.easy: News of the day: The Asylum Project, which I always thought was a bad idea, has become a more interesting place to find workers. I do not think it is impossible to heal a criminal mind. It just needs a harder treatment than they wanted to try. With our direct help and the support of the state, a prison is a much more useful place for experiments.
PrivatizedIntro.6.short: News: the misguided Asylum Project has become an intriguing source of labor. Deviant minds can be reformed, but only with harsher therapy. With our help and the state's blessing, a prison makes a better testing ground.

PrivatizedIntro.7.full: And I — I am doing well. It disconcerts me. My studies continue with great passion that consumes me more than anything I have ever known. Even the dismal fog that looms across this bleak valley fills me with a solemn peace. Yet it is that same calm which causes my unease.
PrivatizedIntro.7.easy: And I, I am doing well. That worries me. I continue my studies with a great passion that fills me more than anything I have ever known. Even the sad fog that hangs over this gray valley gives me a serious kind of peace. But it is this same calm that makes me nervous.
PrivatizedIntro.7.short: And I am doing well, which unsettles me. My studies consume me, and even the valley's dismal fog brings me peace. Yet that very calm makes me uneasy.

PrivatizedIntro.8.full: I must work quickly, as I feel something unseen watches, waiting to emerge from the shadows. I cannot have destiny torn from my grasp just when I reach the pinnacle!
PrivatizedIntro.8.easy: I must work fast, because I feel that something I cannot see is watching me, waiting to come out of the shadows. I cannot let my future be taken from me just when I am about to reach the top!
PrivatizedIntro.8.short: I must work quickly; something unseen watches from the shadows. Destiny will not be torn from me at the pinnacle!

LiberalIntro.4.full: I apologize for the tardiness of my reply, but settling the matters of my inheritance has uncovered distressing revelations that haunt my waking hours. It is terrible. And by terrible, I mean decent, cheerful, and painfully dull. People stroll around this inviting town, greet each other with smiles, and share baked goods. Baked goods! How are they so blind to the dark realities of the world? How did we arrive at such an excruciatingly positive conclusion?
LiberalIntro.4.easy: I am sorry that my answer comes so late, but while taking care of my inheritance, I have found out terrible things that I think about all day. It is terrible. And by terrible, I mean nice, happy, and very boring. People walk around this friendly town, smile at each other, and share cakes and bread. Cakes and bread! How can they not see the dark truth of the world? How did we end up with such a horribly happy result?
LiberalIntro.4.short: Forgive my late reply: settling my inheritance has revealed something terrible. The town is decent, cheerful and painfully dull. People smile and share baked goods! How are they so blind to the world's darkness?

LiberalIntro.5.full: While other institutions across Europe experienced the ravenous strain of overcrowding, our town’s well-funded lunatic asylum proved a luminous model of rehabilitation. Restraints were traded for personal care from the staff and a work release program was expanded for patients eager to assimilate themselves into society once again, with the skills to succeed.
LiberalIntro.5.easy: In other places across Europe, asylums had far too many patients. But our town's asylum had a lot of money, and it became a shining example of how to heal people. Instead of tying patients up, the staff took care of them personally. A program was made bigger to let patients go out to work, so that those who wanted could become part of society again, with the skills to do well.
LiberalIntro.5.short: While asylums across Europe were overcrowded, our well-funded one became a model of rehabilitation: personal care instead of restraints, and work programs to help patients rejoin society.

LiberalIntro.6.full: It is an interesting concept in theory, but one which we know will only end in folly. When I made a brief visit to the Asylum Program (as they now so boldly call it), they even attempted to evaluate me as if I had been admitted. Apparently, the country has turned to more civilized ways to disenfranchise individuals that they fear — not to mention the additional taxes levied against legitimate entrepreneurs such as myself.
LiberalIntro.6.easy: It is an interesting idea in theory, but we know it will only end badly. When I visited the Asylum Program for a short time (that is the proud new name they use), they even tried to examine me as if I were a patient. It seems the country has found more polite ways to take rights away from people they are afraid of. And they also put extra taxes on honest business people like me.
LiberalIntro.6.short: Interesting in theory, but doomed. On a brief visit to the 'Asylum Program', they even tried to evaluate me as a patient. The country has found more civilized ways to sideline those it fears, and to tax entrepreneurs like me.

LiberalIntro.7.full: Like mighty Atlas, I will accept these heavy charges. While I disagree with their methodology, and the expenses of this progressive approach will certainly be a financial burden, access to skilled labor does appeal to me from an efficiency standpoint, if they have the stomach for it.
LiberalIntro.7.easy: Like the strong Atlas in the old stories, I will carry these heavy costs. I do not agree with their methods, and this modern way of doing things will surely cost a lot of money. But being able to find skilled workers is attractive to me, because it is efficient, if they are brave enough for it.
LiberalIntro.7.short: Like Atlas, I will bear these heavy charges. I dislike their methods and the expense, but access to skilled labor is efficient, if they have the stomach for it.

LiberalIntro.8.full: The days are certainly bright here in the valley, but in the end, this light will only make my family's work shine more brilliantly!
LiberalIntro.8.easy: The days in the valley are very bright, but in the end, this light will only make my family's work shine even more!
LiberalIntro.8.short: The valley's days are bright, but that light will only make my family's work shine more brilliantly!

S4Jail1.3.full: Your previous letter appeared rushed and ended with incoherent scribblings. What is this creature business and why have you failed "in the eyes of god" by **aiding the poor thing**? Are you quite sure about your own mental state?
S4Jail1.3.easy: Your last letter seemed to be written in a hurry, and it ended with writing that made no sense. What is this business with the creature? And why do you say you have failed "in the eyes of god" by **helping the poor thing**? Are you really sure that your own mind is healthy?
S4Jail1.3.short: Your last letter was rushed and ended in scribbles. What is this creature business, and how did **aiding the poor thing** fail "in the eyes of god"? Are you sure of your own mind?

S4Jail1.4.full: I have heard a rumor that the **Asylum has expanded**. Perhaps your recent bout of good will spawned this charitable fortune. Whether it is so or not, my friend, I would refer you to it. Not necessarily by way of admitting yourself - unless you feel obliged - but perhaps they could recommend you a remedy to calm your thoughts. I suspect you may require more than a spot of tea and bed rest.
S4Jail1.4.easy: I have heard that the **Asylum has become bigger**. Maybe your recent kindness helped to make this happen. Whether that is true or not, my friend, I suggest you go there. You do not have to stay there as a patient, unless you want to. But maybe they could give you a medicine to calm your thoughts. I think you may need more than a cup of tea and some rest in bed.
S4Jail1.4.short: I hear the **Asylum has expanded**, perhaps thanks to your recent good will. I would refer you to it, not to be admitted, unless you wish, but for a remedy. I suspect you need more than tea and bed rest.

S4Jail1.5.full: What is this nonsense I hear about a hideous **creature left stalking about the countryside** in your region? I ask you only because your recent letters about experiments have been quite unforthcoming.
S4Jail1.5.easy: What is this silly story I hear about an ugly **creature that was left to walk around the countryside** in your region? I only ask because in your recent letters you have told me very little about your experiments.
S4Jail1.5.short: What is this about a hideous **creature left stalking the countryside** near you? Your letters about experiments have said very little.

S4Jail1.6.full: I may disagree with your methods, but I have always attempted to stand by you as an academic. Allowing a monster to wander through the land unchecked, and by many accounts stealing and murdering along the way; why I believe this is sufficient grounds for which to end a friendship.
S4Jail1.6.easy: I may not agree with your methods, but as a scientist, I have always tried to support you. But you let a monster walk freely through the land, and many people say it steals and kills on its way. I believe this is a good enough reason to end a friendship.
S4Jail1.6.short: I have always stood by you as an academic, despite your methods. But letting a monster roam free, by many accounts stealing and murdering, is reason enough to end a friendship.

S4Jail1.7.full: This decision has caused people to **lose faith in the security of the Asylum**, thinking now that madmen are running through the streets. And I certainly don't blame them.
S4Jail1.7.easy: Because of this decision, people **no longer believe that the Asylum is safe**. Now they think mad people are running through the streets. And I certainly do not blame them.
S4Jail1.7.short: People have **lost faith in the security of the Asylum**, fearing madmen roam the streets. I don't blame them.

S4GoodCreature.2.full: I have made peace with the monster, though in so doing I have ensured my place in the fires of hell. With my death, I free my heir from the shackles of sin. My sacrifice will not be in vain! The legacy will transcend me.
S4GoodCreature.2.easy: I have made peace with the monster, but because of this, I will surely burn in hell. When I die, my heir will be free from the chains of sin. My sacrifice will have a purpose! The family's work will live on after me.
S4GoodCreature.2.short: I have made peace with the monster and damned myself. My death frees my heir from sin. The legacy will outlive me!

S4GoodCreature.3.full: So ends the curse upon my family.

S4BadCreature.2.full: I am ruined! Oh how naive I had been to ignore the warnings of my mother and father. They warned me to be vigilant! But I was too proud to believe in superstitious and illogical things such as curses!
S4BadCreature.2.easy: My life is destroyed! Oh, I was so foolish to ignore the warnings of my mother and father. They told me to be careful! But I was too proud to believe in things that make no sense, like curses!
S4BadCreature.2.short: I am ruined! My parents warned me to be vigilant, but I was too proud to believe in curses!

S4BadCreature.3.full: As I slept last night, my estate was breached by a stealthy and merciless beast! And when I awoke, it was to an empty bed and the sound of screaming. I rushed to the window only to see the Creature with his disfigured face carved into a sinister grin, his hands and clothes stained red. He held a burning torch aloft while his black stallion reared. With a swift pull on the reins, he escaped deep into the forest.
S4BadCreature.3.easy: While I slept last night, a quiet and cruel beast broke into my house! When I woke up, the bed beside me was empty and I heard screaming. I ran to the window and saw the Creature. His ugly face had an evil smile, and his hands and clothes were red with blood. He held up a burning torch, and his black horse stood up on its back legs. He pulled the reins quickly and escaped deep into the forest.
S4BadCreature.3.short: Last night a merciless beast broke into my estate. I woke to an empty bed and screaming. From the window I saw the Creature grinning, hands and clothes stained red, a torch held high, before he rode his black stallion into the forest.

S4BadCreature.4.full: Hours later, the pall only darkened as news of my cousins' own tragedies weepingly arrived. A similar fate had befallen their spouses as they were wrenched from the living world by the beast.
S4BadCreature.4.easy: Hours later, things became even darker when sad news came from my cousins. The same thing had happened to their spouses: the beast had taken them from the world of the living.
S4BadCreature.4.short: Hours later came word that my cousins' spouses had met the same fate.

S4BadCreature.5.full: I have only sorrow and hatred left roiling in my heart! I vow to remove that cursed thing from the Earth and reclaim my family's legacy!
S4BadCreature.5.easy: Only sadness and hate are left in my heart! I promise to remove that cursed thing from the Earth and to win back my family's honor!
S4BadCreature.5.short: Only sorrow and hatred remain. I vow to destroy that cursed thing and reclaim my family's legacy!

S4Smug.2.full: I am unsure as to how to proceed. Tonight, I received a smarmy gentlewoman for dinner who introduced herself as the new proprietor of a local warehouse. The purpose of her visit was immediately clear and especially brazen. There was only one reason why anyone would invest in a declining town such as {0} and her resultant smirk was confirmation: illicit trade.
S4Smug.2.easy: I do not know what to do. Tonight, a woman with an unpleasant, false smile came to dinner. She said she was the new owner of a local warehouse. The reason for her visit was clear at once, and very bold. There was only one reason why someone would put money into a dying town like {0}, and her smile told me I was right: illegal trade.
S4Smug.2.short: Tonight a smarmy woman, the new owner of a local warehouse, came to dinner. Why else invest in a declining town like {0}? Her smirk confirmed it: illicit trade.

S4Smug.3.full: The smuggling business is booming as the town's relations with the country deteriorate, this I know. The immediate benefits are enticing, however with any agreement that stretches the law, **there may be consequences.** I'm sure it is nothing life-threatening, but still, is it a gamble worth taking?
S4Smug.3.easy: I know that smuggling is a very good business now, because the town and the country get along worse and worse. The advantages right now are attractive, but with any deal that bends the law, **there may be consequences.** I am sure it is nothing that could kill me, but still, is it worth the risk?
S4Smug.3.short: Smuggling booms as the town and country drift apart. Tempting, but any deal that bends the law **may have consequences.** Is it worth the gamble?

S4Con1.3.full: These charlatans have sentenced me without trial. They say they have evidence of my 'obviously smuggling a large amount of exotic product on the roof of my carriage,' but of course they are unwilling to present it to me or my legal representation.
S4Con1.3.easy: These liars have judged me without a trial. They say they have proof that I was 'clearly smuggling a large amount of foreign goods on the roof of my carriage,' but of course they do not want to show this proof to me or my lawyer.
S4Con1.3.short: These charlatans have sentenced me without trial, claiming evidence of smuggling on my carriage roof, which of course they will not show me or my lawyer.

S4Con1.4.full: I have, due to the pressures of angry villagers who call for vigilante justice, decided against pursuing the slanderous issue as they have not pressed charges. Their faces tell me all that I need to know about how I will be hounded by this public assassination of character.
S4Con1.4.easy: The angry villagers want to punish me themselves, and because of this pressure, I have decided not to fight these lies, because they have not taken me to court. Their faces tell me everything I need to know: this public attack on my good name will follow me everywhere.
S4Con1.4.short: With angry villagers calling for vigilante justice, I have let the slander go, since no charges were pressed. Their faces tell me it will hound me.

S4Con2.3.full: I have been served a notice to appear at the courthouse next week. Can you imagine? The police refuse to present evidence until the trial begins. Of course, my lawyer is the best that money can buy, but these heathens may create farcical evidence that is substantially damning. I am not sure it is worth the risk.
S4Con2.3.easy: I have received a letter that says I must go to the courthouse next week. Can you believe it? The police will not show their proof until the trial starts. Of course, I have the best lawyer that money can buy, but these savages may invent false proof that makes me look very guilty. I am not sure it is worth the risk.
S4Con2.3.short: I am summoned to court next week, and the police will not show their evidence until the trial. My lawyer is the best money can buy, but they may fabricate damning proof. Is it worth the risk?

S4Con2.5.full: You may pay **${0}** to guarantee the success of your case, OR accept the outcome of the trial (which has a 1/3 chance of succeeding).

S4Con2.6.full: Pay the $ to the supply and click here.

S4Con3.3.full: I will not carry on this farce any longer. I admit that I smuggled goods from the docks. This I would do again, I swear, as it is an affront to my sensibilities that I should be so deprived of the resources which I require just to appease these peons.
S4Con3.3.easy: I will not continue this silly game any longer. I admit that I smuggled goods from the docks. I promise I would do it again, because it insults me that I should go without the things I need, just to make these unimportant people happy.
S4Con3.3.short: Enough of this farce: I smuggled goods from the docks, and I would again. Why should I go without what I need to appease these peons?

S4Con3.4.full: It does not matter. The public is too focused on recent events and it is an act that everyone has engaged in. I suspect there will be little to no repercussions.
S4Con3.4.easy: It does not matter. The people are too busy thinking about recent events, and everyone has done the same thing. I think there will be few or no consequences.
S4Con3.4.short: It does not matter. Everyone has done it, and the public is distracted. I expect little to no repercussions.

ThistenseBad.3.full: When the tensions heightened to their breaking point and bloodshed was just moments away, they came to a startling epiphany. They finally realized that they have one thing truly in common.
ThistenseBad.3.easy: When the tension became so great that people were about to kill each other, they suddenly understood something surprising. They finally saw that they have one thing that is really the same for all of them.
ThistenseBad.3.short: On the brink of bloodshed, they had a startling realization: they truly have one thing in common.

ThisTenseGood.3.full: Peace. The townsfolk use this word so flippantly, it has become tawdry. Can there truly be peace without struggle? What is peace for all when I am not at peace myself?
ThisTenseGood.3.easy: Peace. The people of the town use this word so often and so carelessly that it has become cheap. Can there really be peace without a fight? What is peace for everyone when I do not feel peace myself?
ThisTenseGood.3.short: Peace. The townsfolk use the word so carelessly it has become cheap. What is peace for all when I have none myself?

ThisTenseGood.4.full: They have come to an agreement. Peace. Our family's actions, they deemed, were not the cause of their ills. They see how we struggled over the years for them and now they express their thanks. The Memorial is converted to an institute of higher learning in honor of the embrace of modern values.
ThisTenseGood.4.easy: They have agreed. Peace. They decided that our family's actions were not the reason for their problems. They see how hard we worked for them over the years, and now they say thank you. The Memorial is changed into a school for higher learning, to celebrate that they now accept modern values.
ThisTenseGood.4.short: They have agreed on peace, and decided our family was not the cause of their troubles. Now they thank us. The Memorial becomes an institute of higher learning, honoring modern values.

ThisTenseGood.5.full: I am glad that they have pushed past their ignorance, but it is too little too late in my opinion.
ThisTenseGood.5.easy: I am happy that they have moved past their ignorance, but I think it is too little and too late.

CreatureDemands.3.full: To my surprise, the hideous monster could speak, his jaw supported by a crudely stitched black thread which exposed the inner muscle when it moved. In deep, guttural tones, he conveyed his hatred for my grandfather, who had created him and abandoned him, helpless in the wild. "I was forcefully orphaned. Left to fend for myself while his sons and daughters existed in luxury," he groaned.
CreatureDemands.3.easy: To my surprise, the ugly monster could speak. His jaw was held together by rough black thread, and when it moved, you could see the muscle inside. In a deep, rough voice, he told me how much he hated my grandfather, who had made him and then left him alone and helpless in the wild. "I was made into an orphan. I had to look after myself while his sons and daughters lived in luxury," he said with a groan.
CreatureDemands.3.short: To my surprise, the monster could speak, his jaw held by crude black stitches. In a guttural voice he told of his hatred for my grandfather, who created and abandoned him. "I was orphaned while his children lived in luxury," he groaned.

CreatureDemands.4.full: They say the sins of the father are passed on to the children, but rarely does this obligation skip a full generation. "You owe me a great debt, and I am here to demand payment," he stated firmly, and obstructed my escape until he could finish his tale. I was awestruck by his chilling words and the revelation that our family's dark secrets were indeed a reality.
CreatureDemands.4.easy: People say that children pay for the sins of their father, but it rarely happens that a whole generation is skipped. "You owe me a great debt, and I am here to make you pay," he said strongly, and he did not let me escape until he had finished his story. His cold words shocked me, and so did the truth that our family's dark secrets were real.
CreatureDemands.4.short: The sins of the father pass to the children, but rarely skip a generation. "You owe me a great debt, and I am here to collect," he said, blocking my escape. Our family's dark secrets were real.

CreatureDemands.5.full: Cursed into existence despite his decaying form, my grandfather's experiment demanded to live out his days with a faithful companion, another being who can understand the torture of existence. That it was my family's duty to atone for these sins and create it for him!
CreatureDemands.5.easy: He was cursed to live even though his body was rotting. My grandfather's experiment demanded to spend the rest of his life with a loyal partner, another being who could understand how painful it is to exist. He said it was my family's duty to pay for these sins and to make this partner for him!
CreatureDemands.5.short: Cursed with life in a decaying body, my grandfather's experiment demanded a faithful companion who could understand his torment, and said it was my family's duty to create it!

CreatureDemands.6.full: With a final turn, his grotesque figure framed in moonlight, he vowed that if we did not, he would exact a terrible vengeance upon our houses, so that we may know first-hand what torment he has endured!
CreatureDemands.6.easy: He turned one last time, and his terrible body stood in the moonlight. He promised that if we did not do it, he would take terrible revenge on our houses, so that we would learn for ourselves the pain he has lived through!
CreatureDemands.6.short: Turning in the moonlight, he swore that if we failed, he would take terrible vengeance on our houses, so we would know his torment first-hand!

ExpYes.3.full: Success. Oh, if words could adequately describe the crestfallen look on the monstrosity's distorted face as it realized its life was at an end! My servants and I subdued the foul Creature, binding it with rope around its wrists and legs and suspending it upon a felled birch tree with little struggle.
ExpYes.3.easy: Success. Oh, I wish words could describe the sad look on the monster's twisted face when it understood that its life was over! My servants and I overpowered the horrible Creature easily. We tied its wrists and legs with rope and hung it on a birch tree that we had cut down.
ExpYes.3.short: Success! If only words could capture the monster's despair as it realized its end had come. My servants and I subdued it easily, bound it, and hung it from a felled birch.

ExpYes.4.full: Kindled with underbrush and pine needles, I watched as the smoke turned to flame and slowly consumed the monster. First, the frostbitten feet and legs clad in tattered cloth, then the rusted belt-buckle searing through flesh as it fell red-hot into the fire.
ExpYes.4.easy: We lit a fire with small plants and pine needles. I watched as the smoke turned into flames and slowly burned the monster. First its frozen feet and its legs in torn clothes. Then its rusty belt buckle burned through its flesh and fell, red-hot, into the fire.
ExpYes.4.short: We lit underbrush and pine needles, and I watched the flames slowly consume the monster, from its frostbitten feet to the red-hot buckle searing through its flesh.

ExpYes.5.full: It did not scream as it expired, nor did it writhe in agony, as if the pain of its own existence had already overwhelmed all possible sensation. It merely stared in my direction with a forlorn look in its eyes, like all the world had foresaken it. I could not bear the sight. I raised my pistol and shot it dead.
ExpYes.5.easy: It did not scream as it died, and it did not move in pain, as if the pain of its own life had already been stronger than any other feeling. It only looked at me with sad eyes, as if the whole world had left it alone. I could not stand to look at it. I raised my pistol and shot it dead.
ExpYes.5.short: It neither screamed nor writhed, as if its existence had already numbed all pain. It only stared at me, forsaken. I could not bear it, and shot it dead.

ExpNo.3.full: I saw the silhouette of the Creature set against the paleness of the moon. Its hideous features squelched and seethed beneath torn clothing as it bellowed out to the valley before disappearing once again into the mists.
ExpNo.3.easy: I saw the dark shape of the Creature in front of the pale moon. Its ugly face moved and twisted under its torn clothes as it gave a loud cry across the valley. Then it disappeared into the fog again.
ExpNo.3.short: The Creature's silhouette rose against the moon. It bellowed across the valley, then vanished into the mists.

ExpNo.4.full: I reached for my pistol, but found myself abruptly shaken as the image dissipated and I awoke upon my bedroll under the dawn's light. Though my nightmares had grown more vivid with each passing evening, the voyage returned no sign of the Creature. Days hence, I was forced to return empty-handed.
ExpNo.4.easy: I reached for my pistol, but I was suddenly shaken as the picture disappeared, and I woke up in my sleeping bag in the morning light. My nightmares had become clearer every night, but the trip found no sign of the Creature. Days later, I had to go home with nothing.
ExpNo.4.short: I reached for my pistol and woke on my bedroll at dawn. My nightmares grew more vivid, but the journey found no sign of the Creature, and I returned empty-handed.

LiberalEvent.2.full: As I predicted, the Romanian government's expanding social programs have left it unmercifully poor during this brief recession. I have made protective strides to divert my portfolio abroad, so the impact has been negligible. However, the upheaval caused by this Great War has sparked nationalist sentiments and minor rebellions across Transylvania.
LiberalEvent.2.easy: As I said would happen, the Romanian government spent more and more on helping its people, and now, during this short economic crisis, it is terribly poor. I protected myself by moving my money to other countries, so the crisis has hardly hurt me. But the chaos of this Great War has started feelings of national pride and small rebellions across Transylvania.
LiberalEvent.2.short: As I predicted, the government's social programs have left it poor in this recession. My money is safe abroad. But the Great War has stirred nationalism and minor rebellions across Transylvania.

Witchwolfresolution.2.full: Word travels quickly in these parts. For as distant I am from the civilized world, I am equidistant from any meaningful activity to gossip about. While I'm sure you have heard of the recent family tragedy, I wanted you to read it from my own words.

Witchwolfresolution.2.short: News travels fast here, if only for lack of anything else to gossip about. You have surely heard of our recent family tragedy, but I wanted you to hear it from me.

Witchwolfresolution.3.full: As cousins, we frequently sup together when time and weather allows. But woefully, one occasion we chose a night where the wind howled remorselessly and set the locust trees to rapping against the estate windows. Upon this uneasy evening, we spied a great light beaming from the forest, and soon a throng of townspeople rallied around the exterior walls, waving torches and brandishing pitchforks.
Witchwolfresolution.3.easy: As cousins, we often have dinner together when we have time and the weather is good. But sadly, one time we chose a night when the wind howled without mercy and made the trees knock against the windows of the house. On this uneasy evening, we saw a big light shining from the forest. Soon a crowd of townspeople came together around the outside walls, waving torches and pitchforks.
Witchwolfresolution.3.short: We cousins often dine together. One night, as the wind howled and branches rapped at the windows, we saw a great light in the forest, and soon a crowd with torches and pitchforks gathered outside our walls.

Witchwolfresolution.4.full: The townspeople blamed us for bringing a blight of witchcraft upon their town. Tonight, they demanded a sacrifice and no amount of persuasion would slake their thirst for blood. As the hounds kept them at bay, we were forced to make a sanguine decision that would haunt us for the remainder of our days.
Witchwolfresolution.4.easy: The townspeople said we had brought witchcraft to their town like a disease. Tonight, they wanted a sacrifice, and nothing we said could stop their wish for blood. While the dogs kept them away, we had to make a bloody decision that would stay with us for the rest of our lives.
Witchwolfresolution.4.short: They blamed us for bringing witchcraft upon the town and demanded a sacrifice. As the hounds held them back, we were forced to make a decision that would haunt us forever.

WallEvent.1.full: **Memorial to the Past for the Future**

WallEvent.2.full: As expected - and as I've relayed to you so amusingly in the past - the town is not seeing adequate support for their memorial. This time, however, I was distinctly unamused to have my experimentations interrupted just as I had secured a moment's peace. Only yesterday, well-dressed representatives from the local government (mind you, as well-dressed as a fop with a decade's old sense of fashion can be) visited the estate in person to ask for my assistance.
WallEvent.2.easy: As I expected, and as I have told you in funny letters before, the town does not get enough support for its memorial. But this time I was not amused at all when my experiments were stopped, just when I had found a moment of peace. Only yesterday, well-dressed people from the local government came to my house to ask for my help. (Well, as well dressed as a vain man can be when his fashion is ten years old.)
WallEvent.2.short: As expected, the town lacks support for its memorial. This time I was not amused when officials, dressed in decade-old fashion, interrupted my experiments to ask for help.

WallEvent.3.full: When I pressed as to the actual purpose of our donations, they act as a parakeet with its cage door rattled; wildly gesticulating and talking vaguely about eliminating all possible superstition and influence from the town to make it prosperous again. Quite unlikely, I would say.
WallEvent.3.easy: When I asked what our money was really for, they acted like a parrot when you shake its cage: they waved their arms wildly and talked vaguely about removing all superstition and outside influence from the town, so that it could become rich again. That is not very likely, I would say.
WallEvent.3.short: Asked what our donations were for, they flapped like a startled parakeet, vaguely promising to rid the town of all superstition and influence to make it prosperous. Unlikely, I'd say.

WallEvent.4.full: My dealings with the local Romani merchants have made it clear that whatever the town's petty inclinations, the memorial will have a deep affect on their trade. The Romani do not wish to leave the region, but will do so if pressed.
WallEvent.4.easy: From my business with the local Romani traders, it is clear that whatever small-minded ideas the town has, the memorial will have a strong effect on their trade. The Romani do not want to leave the region, but they will if they are pushed.
WallEvent.4.short: My dealings with the Romani merchants make it clear that the memorial will hurt their trade. They do not wish to leave, but will if pressed.
