LiberalEvent2.3.full: Outrageous! Our representative in parliament returns our correspondence with a sharp rebuke of our attempts to use our influence to alter the purely democratic process. Would they really leave this matter to popular opinion? This ignoble disrespect is more than my superior scientific mind can endure!
LiberalEvent2.3.easy: Shocking! Our representative in parliament answered our letters by sharply criticizing us for trying to use our influence to change the purely democratic process. Do they really want to let the people decide this question? This lack of respect is more than my superior scientific mind can accept!
LiberalEvent2.3.short: Outrageous! Our representative in parliament rebukes us for using our influence on the democratic process. Leave this to popular opinion? My superior mind cannot endure such disrespect!

LiberalEvent2.4.full: No, it is clear they are attempting to weasel money from our coffers. His insinuation that we have not yet provided sufficient impetus to sway his political decisiveness is well understood. If we would like to see our choice become law, we need to offer a bribe.
LiberalEvent2.4.easy: No, it is clear that they are trying to get money out of us with tricks. We understand very well what he means: we have not yet given him enough reason to make the political decision we want. If we want our choice to become law, we need to offer a bribe.
LiberalEvent2.4.short: No, they are clearly fishing for money. His hint is plain: if we want our choice to become law, we must offer a bribe.

LiberalEvent2.5.full: A bribe of **${0}** will be sufficient. Otherwise we can allow the people to make the choice.

LiberalEventA.3.full: To our chagrin, the choice is left to the democratic process. We are resigned to the results.
LiberalEventA.3.easy: To our disappointment, the people will decide by vote. We accept the results.

LiberalEventA.4.full: We are happy to see that our contributions to society still hold sway.
LiberalEventA.4.easy: We are happy to see that our gifts to society still have influence.

LiberalEventA.5.full: A new "income tax" has been created to reduce the proper stratification of society by wealth seen across Transylvania. It naturally disgusts me, but I find it better than the alternative.
LiberalEventA.5.easy: A new "income tax" has been made to reduce the natural difference between rich and poor that you can see across Transylvania. Of course it disgusts me, but I think it is better than the other choice.
LiberalEventA.5.short: A new "income tax" aims to narrow the proper divide between rich and poor. It disgusts me, but beats the alternative.

LiberalEventA.6.full: Each player **must pay $1** to the supply.

LiberalEventB.3.full: To our chagrin, the choice is left to the democratic process. We are resigned to the results.
LiberalEventB.3.easy: To our disappointment, the people will decide by vote. We accept the results.

LiberalEventB.4.full: We are happy to see that our contributions to society still hold sway.
LiberalEventB.4.easy: We are happy to see that our gifts to society still have influence.

LiberalEventB.5.full: The Nationalist movement within parliament is successful. I find myself unmoved by the horrifying details of conditions within the Asylum worsening and deportations of various peoples based on their ethnic group or religious views. Politics. It will sort itself out.
LiberalEventB.5.easy: The Nationalist movement in parliament has won. I do not care about the horrible reports that life in the Asylum is getting worse, or that people are sent out of the country because of their ethnic group or their religion. Politics. It will fix itself.
LiberalEventB.5.short: The Nationalists have won in parliament. Reports of worsening conditions in the Asylum and deportations by ethnicity or faith leave me unmoved. Politics. It will sort itself out.

LiberalEventB.6.full: **Each player must return their {0} tile to the Scenario box.**

SmugEvent.1.full: **Carefully pick up the Storybook device and hand it to the player with the least VP.**

SmugEvent.2.full: *If there is a tie, hand this to the one who was later in turn order in the previous round.* **This passage is read in full view of all players.**

SmugEvent.4.full: My cousins and I have come to an agreement as of earlier today; one that I believe we should have spoken of much sooner. The topic came about as we were discussing our various sundry interests, and like the pendulum tick of a longcase clock, our words kept returning to the stifling environment in which we now found ourselves.
SmugEvent.4.easy: My cousins and I made an agreement earlier today. I think we should have talked about it much sooner. The subject came up while we were talking about our different interests. Like the swinging of a tall clock, our words kept coming back to the closed, airless place where we now found ourselves.
SmugEvent.4.short: Today my cousins and I reached an overdue agreement. Our talk kept swinging back, like a clock's pendulum, to the stifling place we now found ourselves in.

SmugEvent.5.full: I'll be quick with it; we resolved to turn a resounding negative into a boon!
SmugEvent.5.easy: I will say it quickly: we decided to turn something very bad into something good!

SmugEvent.6.full: One of the distinct bonuses of being located near an entire town surrounded by a large wall is that it provides excellent controls for an experiment. Without the means to escape, our scientific methods could be indulged with little consequence.
SmugEvent.6.easy: One great advantage of living near a whole town with a big wall around it is that it is perfect for controlling an experiment. Without a way to escape, we could use our scientific methods freely, with few consequences.
SmugEvent.6.short: A walled town makes an excellent controlled experiment. With no means of escape, our scientific methods could be indulged freely.

SmugEvent.8.full: Retrieve the 3 **Collaborative Experiments** from the Scenario box.

SmugEvent.9.full: The player with the **least VP** now chooses the **type** of Collaborative Experiment that all players will be working towards. This determines which of the three Experiments will be unleashed. *To be completed, this Experiment will require multiple players to complete Experiments of that type this round.*

SmugEventA.2.full: To properly introduce the creation to a captive audience, **{0}** Collaboration {icon:S2_CollaborativeToken} tokens must be gained by completing

SmugEventA.7.full: Each player can only gain **1** Collaboration token {icon:S2_CollaborativeToken}.

SmugEventA.8.full: The player who gains the most {icon:S2_CollaborativeToken} tokens will gain an additional **4VP.**

SmugEventA.10.full: **Injecting an Agitated Gorilla with Hormones and Radium**

SmugEventA.12.full: **A Robot Servant That Prepares Meals with Lasers**

SmugEventA.13.full: Experiment face-up on the table. Discard the remaining Collaborative Experiments.

SmugEventA.14.full: Then, retrieve **{0}** {icon:S2_CollaborativeToken} tokens and place them on the Collaborative Experiment.

SmugEventA.15.full: **WARNING: COMPLETING THIS EXPERIMENT WILL DEFINITELY DESTROY CITY HALL. MEANING THAT YOU WILL NOT HAVE TO PLACE YOUR SELF TOKEN ONTO IT. ALSO, IT MAY HAVE OTHER, MORE DIRE CONSEQUENCES.**

SmugConsequence.4.full: **Please choose your name and add it to the ledger:**

S4Con2A.3.full: Despite circumstantial evidence, the town's courts were unable to reconcile their case with my unusual investment practices. Several witnesses attested to my family's eccentric habits, and while it does not put the courts at ease, the argument is compelling enough for them to drop the charges without fines.
S4Con2A.3.easy: The proof was not direct, and the town's courts could not make their case fit with my unusual ways of investing money. Several witnesses said that my family has strange habits. The courts were not completely happy with this, but the argument was strong enough for them to drop the charges without any fines.
S4Con2A.3.short: The evidence was only circumstantial, and witnesses to my family's eccentric habits persuaded the court to drop the charges without fines.

S4Con2A.6.full: Despite circumstantial evidence, the town's courts were unable to reconcile their case with my unusual investment practices. Several witnesses attested to my family's eccentric habits, and while it does not put the courts at ease, the argument is compelling enough for them to drop the charges without fines.
S4Con2A.6.easy: The proof was not direct, and the town's courts could not make their case fit with my unusual ways of investing money. Several witnesses said that my family has strange habits. The courts were not completely happy with this, but the argument was strong enough for them to drop the charges without any fines.
S4Con2A.6.short: The evidence was only circumstantial, and witnesses to my family's eccentric habits persuaded the court to drop the charges without fines.

S4Con2A.9.full: You should have seen the unsteadiness of the case they brought against me! Several witnesses attested to my connection to the local smuggling ring (absurd), but the bedraggled individuals could not even keep their own stories straight.
S4Con2A.9.easy: You should have seen how weak their case against me was! Several witnesses said I was connected to the local smugglers (silly), but these dirty, tired people could not even tell their own stories the same way twice.
S4Con2A.9.short: Their case was so shaky! Witnesses tied me to the local smugglers (absurd), but could not keep their own stories straight.

S4Con2A.10.full: We are dealing with the simple-minded, however. The judge, in their folly, determined that scant evidence was significant enough to damn me. While the court costs are minor and the fines insignificant, the resulting public backlash will certainly hamper my ability to complete any work in peace.
S4Con2A.10.easy: But we are dealing with simple people. The judge, foolishly, decided that the little proof they had was enough to find me guilty. The court costs are small and the fines are not important, but the angry reaction of the public will certainly make it hard for me to finish any work in peace.
S4Con2A.10.short: But we deal with simpletons: the judge found scant evidence enough to damn me. The fines are trivial, but the public backlash will disturb my work.

S4Con2A.13.full: My representation was easily able to refute the validity of several eyewitness accounts from slipshod drunkards, but the court proceedings dragged on for several months.
S4Con2A.13.easy: My lawyers easily showed that the stories of several witnesses, who were careless drunks, could not be trusted. But the court process went on for several months.
S4Con2A.13.short: My lawyers easily discredited the drunken witnesses, but the case dragged on for months.

S4Con2A.14.full: Ultimately, the blasted dullards had not a leg to stand on and were forced to drop the case entirely. While the court costs are minor and the fines insignificant, the time wasted in this extended defense and the indigestion I have endured has caused my work to suffer.
S4Con2A.14.easy: In the end, the stupid fools had nothing to support their case and had to drop it completely. The court costs are small and the fines are not important, but the time I lost in this long defense, and the stomach pains I had, have hurt my work.
S4Con2A.14.short: In the end the dullards had no case and dropped it. The costs were trivial, but the wasted time and my indigestion have hurt my work.

TensionBonus.3.full: The player with the second-most Experiments will also receive this Upgrade.

TensionBonus.5.full: **Also,** any player who has completed their **Occult Journal Track gains 3VP**.

LiberalBonus.3.full: The player who has the second-most Experiments also gains this Upgrade.

SmugEvent2A.3.full: Four dead and several injured after a calamity of epic proportions occurred yesterday in our fair city of {0}. While the cause of the sudden implosion and subsequent spread of detritus remains unknown, officials confirm the complete destruction of the Town Hall.
SmugEvent2A.3.easy: Four people are dead and several are hurt after a huge disaster yesterday in our beautiful city of {0}. Nobody knows yet why the building suddenly fell in on itself and threw pieces everywhere, but officials confirm that the Town Hall is completely destroyed.
SmugEvent2A.3.short: Four dead and several injured after yesterday's disaster in {0}. The cause of the sudden collapse is unknown, but the Town Hall is completely destroyed.

SmugEvent2A.4.full: The player with the most Collaboration tokens {icon:S2_CollaborativeToken}** gains 4VP**.

SmugEvent2A.5.full: Players that have already visited the Town Hall gain a small bonus:

SmugEvent2B.2.full: I knew it would never amount to anything! My cousins do not share the same illumination, the same pioneering spirit that I exhibit! They would rather languish in gluttony and submit to the oppressive state. I see their bellies grow rotund in their slothful lethargy, their porcine features stuffed into last year's fashion by couturiers no doubt pushed to the brink.
SmugEvent2B.2.easy: I knew it would never become anything! My cousins do not have the same clear mind or the same spirit of discovery that I have! They prefer to sit around eating too much and to obey the cruel state. I see their bellies grow round because they are so lazy, and their pig-like bodies pushed into last year's fashion by tailors who are surely at the end of their patience.
SmugEvent2B.2.short: I knew it would come to nothing! My cousins lack my vision and pioneering spirit. They would rather grow fat and lazy and bow to the state, their porcine forms squeezed into last year's fashions.

SmugEvent2B.3.full: Perhaps it was good that they could not complete it. At least that way the experiment could not be considered a *failure*!
SmugEvent2B.3.easy: Maybe it was good that they could not finish it. At least then nobody could call the experiment a *failure*!

SmugEvent2B.4.full: Any player who gained a Collaboration token {icon:S2_CollaborativeToken} gains **1 Knowledge of their choice**

SmugEvent2B.6.full: and then returns the token to the box.

SmugEvent2B.7.full: Any player who does not have a Collaboration token {icon:S2_CollaborativeToken} is not dedicated to the craft and **loses 2VP**.

SmugEvent2B.8.full: The player with the most Collaboration tokens {icon:S2_CollaborativeToken} **gains 4VP**. *If there is a tie, no one receives this bonus.*

SmugEvent2Aa.3.full: The Bank was the next target of our experiment's seemingly arbitrary rage. Perhaps it was the promise of glittering treasures within that caught its attention; or more likely, it was the soldier stationed out front who fired upon it repeatedly with a handgun.
SmugEvent2Aa.3.easy: The Bank was the next target of our experiment's anger, which seemed to have no reason. Maybe the treasures shining inside caught its attention. Or, more likely, it was the soldier standing in front, who shot at it many times with a handgun.
SmugEvent2Aa.3.short: The Bank was next. Perhaps the treasures within drew it, or, more likely, the soldier out front who kept shooting at it.

SmugEvent2Aa.4.full: Either way, the soldier was given a premature burial under the falling stone and girders that burst from the structure as it was torn apart quite violently and the path of rampage continued.
SmugEvent2Aa.4.easy: In any case, the soldier was buried too early, under the falling stones and steel beams that flew out of the building as it was violently torn apart. And the path of destruction went on.
SmugEvent2Aa.4.short: Either way, the soldier was buried under the falling stone as the building was torn apart, and the rampage continued.

SmugEvent2Aa.5.full: Click to see if the Experiment's rampage continues...

SmugEvent2aa.3.full: It was unfortunate to see the library - however limited its collection and provisional its overall design - collapse into a pile of dust, books, and blood.
SmugEvent2aa.3.easy: It was sad to see the library fall into a pile of dust, books, and blood, even though it did not have many books and was only built simply.
SmugEvent2aa.3.short: Sadly, the modest library collapsed into dust, books and blood.

SmugEvent2aa.4.full: Our creation paused for a brief moment, the entirety of its form shaking violently in the center of the town. Suddenly, with a blinding flash and a resultant shockwave which shattered the windows of all nearby business, it exploded. The vibrant display was admittedly so engrossing that for a moment I imagined the townsfolk had simply been stunned into silence. At least until several spontaneously burst into flames.
SmugEvent2aa.4.easy: Our creation stopped for a short moment, and its whole body shook violently in the center of the town. Suddenly, with a very bright flash and a wave of force that broke the windows of all the shops nearby, it exploded. I must admit, the colorful show was so exciting that for a moment I thought the townspeople were just too surprised to speak. That was until several of them suddenly caught fire.
SmugEvent2aa.4.short: Our creation paused, shaking violently in the town center, then exploded in a blinding flash that shattered every nearby window. For a moment the townsfolk seemed simply stunned, until several burst into flames.

SmugEvent2aa.5.full: With nowhere to escape, the remaining townsfolk desperately attempted to douse the fires and rush to the aide of the injured. We watched from our cliffside seclusion as pandemonium gripped the populace.
SmugEvent2aa.5.easy: With no way to escape, the other townspeople tried desperately to put out the fires and to help the hurt people. From our quiet place on the cliff, we watched as panic took over the people.
SmugEvent2aa.5.short: Trapped, the townsfolk fought the fires and tended the injured, while we watched the chaos from our cliffside.

SmugEvent2aa.6.full: Move the {icon:AngryMob_Icon} Marker **3 spaces** to the left.

S4Kill2.2.full: Each player takes a voting token into their fist and secretly chooses a side. When all players have chosen, simultaneously reveal your votes.

S4Kill2.5.full: Tally the vote count *(ties are broken by the player who went last this round).*

SmugEventEnd.3.full: Disappointingly, the action ceased just as quickly as it had begun.
SmugEventEnd.3.easy: Sadly, the action stopped as quickly as it had started.

SmugEventEnd.4.full: Our Gorilla, now grown to the size of a small home, beat its mighty fists against its chest one last time with a roar that rattled our inner ears even from nearly a kilometer away. It then struggled for balance.
SmugEventEnd.4.easy: Our Gorilla, which was now as big as a small house, beat its strong fists against its chest one last time. It roared so loudly that our ears shook, even though we were almost a kilometer away. Then it started to lose its balance.
SmugEventEnd.4.short: Our Gorilla, now the size of a small house, beat its chest one last time with a roar we felt a kilometer away, then began to sway.

SmugEventEnd.5.full: The Fabric swirled one last time in the air, launching a pedestrian with such force that their ragdoll form cleared the exterior wall of the town. A streak of electricity flashed once upon its surface and it began to lazily descend as if caught in a gust of wind.
SmugEventEnd.5.easy: The Fabric turned in the air one last time and threw a person walking by so hard that their body flew over the outside wall of the town like a doll. Electricity flashed once across its surface, and it began to fall down slowly, as if it were carried by the wind.
SmugEventEnd.5.short: The Fabric whirled one last time, flinging a pedestrian over the town wall. A spark crossed its surface, and it drifted slowly down.

SmugEventEnd.6.full: Our Robot expeled a burst of steam that sent a nearby crowd screaming and clutching at their eyes, before its clockwork form began to seize up in the center of the street.
SmugEventEnd.6.easy: Our Robot let out a burst of steam that made a crowd nearby scream and hold their eyes. Then its clockwork body began to stop moving in the middle of the street.
SmugEventEnd.6.short: Our Robot blasted steam into a screaming crowd, then its clockwork seized up in the middle of the street.

SmugEventEnd.7.full: Our creation settled lifelessly to the ground, bits of metal, wood, and smoldering flesh strewn about the cobblestones where it lay. While we would have enjoyed seeing our experiment tested at the highest level, the cloud of smoke and the destruction left in its wake were acceptable.
SmugEventEnd.7.easy: Our creation fell to the ground without life. Pieces of metal, wood, and burning flesh lay all over the stone street where it fell. We would have liked to see our experiment tested to the very end, but the cloud of smoke and the destruction it left behind were good enough.
SmugEventEnd.7.short: Our creation fell lifeless amid scattered metal, wood and smoldering flesh. We had hoped for more, but the smoke and destruction were acceptable.

SmugEventEnd.8.full: The townsfolk scrambled through the streets trying to put out fires that popped up throughout the town as we enjoyed a warm coffee from our secluded viewing location and discussed the results. Science can be so  satisfying.
SmugEventEnd.8.easy: The townspeople ran through the streets, trying to put out the fires that started all over town, while we enjoyed a warm coffee in our quiet place and talked about the results. Science can be so satisfying.
SmugEventEnd.8.short: As the townsfolk ran to put out fires, we sipped coffee from our hideaway and discussed the results. Science can be so satisfying.

SmugEventEnd.9.full: Move the {icon:AngryMob_Icon} Marker **{0}** to the left.

LiberalTaxes.2.full: Taxes upon an inheritance? Have you heard of such a thing? It appears that the county exchequer has levied an estate tax upon the wealthier citizenry.
LiberalTaxes.2.easy: Taxes on an inheritance? Have you ever heard of such a thing? It seems that the county's treasury now takes a tax on the property of richer citizens when they die.
LiberalTaxes.2.short: Taxes on an inheritance? The county now levies an estate tax on the wealthy!

LiberalTaxes.3.full: Our mid-morning bout of croquet was unduly interrupted by the arrival of the news. This progressive poppycock was so destructive to my ability to run the hoop that my spouse was able to peg out well before I was competitive. Does an estate mean nothing to these leeches?
LiberalTaxes.3.easy: The news arrived during our game of croquet in the middle of the morning and disturbed it. This modern nonsense upset me so much that I could not hit the ball through the hoops, and my spouse finished the game long before I had a chance. Does a family's property mean nothing to these bloodsuckers?
LiberalTaxes.3.short: The news ruined our morning croquet; I was so rattled my spouse finished long before me. Does an estate mean nothing to these leeches?

LiberalTaxes.4.full: They claim it is necessary to ensure the Asylum and various other modern amenities like public schools and health care are provided. Perhaps if they ran these facilities profitably they would not have to bleed their constituents.
LiberalTaxes.4.easy: They say it is necessary to pay for the Asylum and other modern services like public schools and health care. Maybe if they ran these places so that they made money, they would not need to take so much from the people.
LiberalTaxes.4.short: They say it pays for the Asylum, schools and health care. If they ran these profitably, they would not need to bleed us.

LiberalTaxes.5.full: It took several days of constitutional rest for my spouse and I to recover from the shock of this intrusion into our financial affairs!
LiberalTaxes.5.easy: My spouse and I needed several days of rest and walks to recover from the shock of this attack on our money!

LiberalTaxes2.3.full: In the coming weeks, several armed men along with a single gentleman dressed in a brown sack suit arrived at the estates of my cousins who chose to avoid tax collection.
LiberalTaxes2.3.easy: In the following weeks, several men with weapons and one man in a simple brown suit came to the houses of my cousins who had chosen not to pay their taxes.
LiberalTaxes2.3.short: In the following weeks, armed men and a man in a brown suit visited the cousins who had avoided the tax.

LiberalTaxes2.4.full: Any player who **paid their taxes** in full, gains **{0}VP** immediately.

LiberalTaxes2.5.full: Any player who **refused** to pay taxes may immediately make up the difference by returning **1 Ingredient OR 1 Estate Upgrade to the supply for every 2 Estate Upgrades they own.** If they cannot or choose not to perform this action, they must **place their Self on the City Hall immediately and Lose {0}VP**. *This token performs no action this round.*

WallEvent2.2.full: The effect of our decision was not immediately apparent, but I could discern that the townspeople were grateful for support from the aristocracy.
WallEvent2.2.easy: The effect of our decision could not be seen at once, but I could tell that the townspeople were thankful for the support of the rich families.

WallEvent2.3.full: In the coming weeks, the traveling caravans kept their distance, unsure of the new direction the town had taken. However, on the occasions that I frequented their motley convoy they pledged to return again at a later date and reward the members of our family with weaker hearts.
WallEvent2.3.easy: In the following weeks, the traveling caravans stayed away, because they were not sure about the town's new direction. But when I visited their colorful group of wagons, they promised to come back later and reward the members of our family who have weaker hearts.
WallEvent2.3.short: For weeks the caravans kept their distance, unsure of the town's new direction. But when I visited, they promised to return and reward the members of our family with weaker hearts.

WallEvent2.5.full: The Romani caravans, while still apprehensive, seem to have recognized the sincerity of our deeds, or the depth of our pockets. Whether trust has been gained or a mutually beneficial arrangement, I suspect they will return again at a later date and reward the members of our family with weaker hearts.
WallEvent2.5.easy: The Romani caravans are still worried, but they seem to see that our actions are honest, or that we have a lot of money. Maybe they trust us now, or maybe it is just a deal that is good for both sides. In any case, I think they will come back later and reward the members of our family who have weaker hearts.
WallEvent2.5.short: The wary Romani seem to recognize our sincerity, or our deep pockets. I suspect they will return and reward the members of our family with weaker hearts.

WallEvent2.7.full: All players with money in their hand must pay it to the supply to gain a **Memorial Brick**. They immediately gain **2VP** and **lose 1 {icon:Creepy_Icon}.**

WallEvent2.8.full: Retrieve the **Market tokens** {icon:S2_MarketToken} from the Scenario box.

WallEvent2.9.full: Any player who did **not** spend $1 for a brick, gains **1 Occult Knowledge** and a **Market token **{icon:S2_MarketToken}.

WallEvent2.10.full: **For the remainder of the game, at the end of each round there is a chance that the Romani will visit the town and offer goods to players with a {icon:S2_MarketToken} token.**

WallEvent2.11.full: All players with money in their hand must pay it to the supply to gain a **Memorial Brick**. They immediately gain **2VP** and **lose 2 {icon:Creepy_Icon}.**

WallEvent2.12.full: Retrieve the **Market tokens **{icon:S2_MarketToken} from the Scenario box.

WallEvent2.14.full: **For the remainder of the game, at the end of each round, there is a chance that the Romani will visit the town and offer goods to players with a {icon:S2_MarketToken} token.**

Caravansery.2.full: A brightly colored carriage arrived today. Its occupants quickly dislodged themselves and through a series of minor alterations, the shutters of the wagon were opened to create an informal display counter with a fabric awning above. Against the monochrome and misty gray stone of the castle walls, the impromptu market looked positively alluring.
Caravansery.2.easy: A carriage with bright colors arrived today. The people inside got out quickly, and with a few small changes, they opened the shutters of the wagon to make a simple counter to show their goods, with a cloth roof above it. Next to the gray, foggy stone walls of the castle, the little market looked very attractive.
Caravansery.2.short: A brightly colored carriage arrived today and opened into a market stall under a fabric awning, alluring against the gray castle walls.

Caravansery.3.full: In turn order, any player with a **Market token** {icon:S2_MarketToken} may choose to purchase **any number** of goods at the Traveling Caravan:

Caravansery.4.full: **Pay $1: Gain 1 Ingredient or 1 Knowledge of your choice.**

Caravansery.5.full: *We note that the caravan is always wandering and is never guaranteed to return again.*

EssentialSalts.2.full: The package has arrived! The vial of essential salts is well and fully intact with a cork stopper firmly fastened. It is as diminutive as I expected, with a small tag attached displaying an Enochian phrase, "Yogg-Sothoth Neblod Zin."
EssentialSalts.2.easy: The package has arrived! The small bottle of essential salts is complete and not broken, with a cork firmly in the top. It is as small as I expected. A little label on it shows words in the Enochian language: "Yogg-Sothoth Neblod Zin."
EssentialSalts.2.short: The package has arrived! The tiny corked vial of essential salts is intact, its tag bearing an Enochian phrase: "Yogg-Sothoth Neblod Zin."

EssentialSalts.3.full: Afternoon Note: Initial experiments have proven promising. A rabbit, only days since skinned and left to drain. The formulae recommended by Joseph Curwen caused a green-black smoke to arise around the carcass. But, moments later, I saw the beating of the animal's once-dead heart as it began to struggle against its bindings! Life from death!
EssentialSalts.3.easy: Afternoon note: The first experiments look good. I used a rabbit that had been skinned only a few days before and left so its blood would run out. The formula that Joseph Curwen recommended made green-black smoke rise around the dead body. But a few moments later, I saw the animal's dead heart beating again, and it began to fight against the ropes that held it! Life from death!
EssentialSalts.3.short: Afternoon note: promising results. Curwen's formula raised green-black smoke around a days-dead, skinned rabbit, and moments later its heart beat and it struggled against its bindings! Life from death!

EssentialSalts.4.full: With the creature lain to rest, there is nothing preventing me from achieving what I have desired for so long! To resurrect my love and return to the happiness we once shared!
EssentialSalts.4.easy: Now that the creature is dead, nothing can stop me from doing what I have wanted for so long! To bring my love back to life and to be as happy as we once were!
EssentialSalts.4.short: With the creature laid to rest, nothing stops me from resurrecting my love and the happiness we shared!

EssentialCons.3.full: Whether for love or purpose - I know not which drove my decision - I broke into the mausoleum housing my spouse and applied the solution to their skeletal features. *Following the exact recipe for the formulae proved difficult, but I was able to make due with local alternatives.*
EssentialCons.3.easy: Maybe it was for love, maybe it was for my work. I do not know which one made me decide. I broke into the family grave where my spouse lay and put the mixture on their bones. *It was hard to follow the formula exactly, but I was able to use local ingredients instead.*
EssentialCons.3.short: For love or for purpose, I broke into my spouse's mausoleum and applied the solution to their bones. *The exact formula was hard to follow, but local substitutes served.*

EssentialCons.4.full: With a billow of emerald smoke, I saw the features of my long-dead spouse reform into the perfect form I remembered from my youth. I had done it!
EssentialCons.4.easy: In a cloud of green smoke, I saw the face of my spouse, who had been dead for so long, take shape again, exactly as I remembered it from when I was young. I had done it!
EssentialCons.4.short: In a cloud of emerald smoke, my long-dead spouse's features reformed, perfect as I remembered. I had done it!

EssentialCons.5.full: I could scarcely trust my own senses. It worked? And without any defects visible or otherwise?
EssentialCons.5.easy: I could hardly believe my own eyes. It worked? And without any problems that I could see, or any others?

EssentialCons.6.full: I embraced them, and though they were startled by the decades' difference in our ages, they returned the embrace. I am a genius!
EssentialCons.6.easy: I held them in my arms. They were surprised that I was now so many years older than them, but they held me too. I am a genius!

EssentialCons.7.full: However, I find that their temperament is uneven. On one particular evening, they suddenly burst open the doors of our carriage and fled into an alleyway before I could recover my senses enough to make chase.
EssentialCons.7.easy: But I see that their moods change suddenly. One evening, they suddenly threw open the doors of our carriage and ran into a small street, before I could think clearly enough to follow them.
EssentialCons.7.short: But their temper is uneven. One evening they burst from our carriage and fled down an alley before I could follow.

EssentialCons.8.full: I observed in abject horror as their neck spun unnaturally around to face me while their body remained stationary. Their feral lips were covered in blood and the fresh body of some unfortunate man lay eviscerated on the cobblestones, their insides glistening in the haze of a crescent moon.
EssentialCons.8.easy: I watched in complete horror as their head turned all the way around to look at me, while their body did not move. Their wild lips were covered in blood, and the body of some poor man lay cut open on the stone street. His insides were shining in the light of a thin moon.
EssentialCons.8.short: To my horror, their head turned fully around to face me, lips bloodied, above the eviscerated body of some poor man glistening under the crescent moon.

EssentialCons.9.full: Generally though, they are back to their normal selves.
EssentialCons.9.easy: But most of the time, they are like they used to be.

EssentialCons.10.full: Any player who chose to perform the resurrection **regains their Spouse** from the game box and places it in their Quarters.

EssentialSaltsRes.3.short: For love or for purpose, I broke into my spouse's mausoleum and applied the solution to their bones. *The exact formula was hard to follow, but local substitutes served.*

EssentialSaltsRes.4.full: With a billow of emerald smoke, I saw the features of my long-dead spouse begin to reform.
EssentialSaltsRes.4.easy: In a cloud of green smoke, I saw the face of my spouse, who had been dead for so long, begin to take shape again.

EssentialSaltsRes.5.full: However, the hideous silhouette that emerged from within the shroud of electrical mist only vaguely resembled my lost love. Their skin oozed about their unsettling musculature while they rose to their feet with a hunched back and a stiff gait on legs of different lengths.
EssentialSaltsRes.5.easy: But the ugly shape that came out of the electric fog only looked a little like my lost love. Their skin moved strangely over their frightening muscles as they stood up. Their back was bent, and they walked stiffly on legs that were not the same length.
EssentialSaltsRes.5.short: But the hideous figure that emerged from the mist barely resembled my love: oozing skin, a hunched back, and a stiff gait on uneven legs.

EssentialSaltsRes.6.full: I spoke to them and though the torment of existence wore heavily on their shambling form, my spouse returned a toothless smile and dutifully obeyed my commands.
EssentialSaltsRes.6.easy: I spoke to them. Even though the pain of living was heavy on their clumsy body, my spouse gave me a smile without teeth and obeyed my orders faithfully.
EssentialSaltsRes.6.short: When I spoke, my tormented spouse gave a toothless smile and dutifully obeyed.

EssentialSaltsRes.7.full: Any player who chose to perform the resurrection **gains a Caretaker from Lost** and **2 {icon:Creepy_Icon}.**

EssentialSaltsRes.8.full: *If you cannot gain a Caretaker from Lost, **gain 2VP, 1 {icon:Bodies_Icon}, and 2 {icon:Creepy_Icon}** instead.*

WitchIsolationResolution.3.full: The townsfolk are wary of me. As well they should be. While I do not hold grudges against simpletons unworthy of my time, the death of my parent is a wound that festers deep within me and I feel no sense of pride in this place.
WitchIsolationResolution.3.easy: The townspeople do not trust me. And they are right not to. I do not hate simple people who are not worth my time, but the death of my parent is a wound that hurts deep inside me, and I do not feel proud of this place.
WitchIsolationResolution.3.short: The townsfolk are wary of me, as they should be. My parent's death festers within me, and I feel no pride in this place.

WitchIsolationResolution.4.full: I am left to my own dark devices, sequestered in my study with dusty tomes and ancient scrolls. My work is my rebellion against their oppression. If the city burns, I will not fan the flames, but I will watch it roast.
WitchIsolationResolution.4.easy: I am left alone with my dark plans, closed in my study with old dusty books and ancient scrolls. My work is my fight against their cruel control. If the city burns, I will not make the fire bigger, but I will watch it burn.
WitchIsolationResolution.4.short: Alone in my study with ancient tomes, my work is my rebellion. If the city burns, I will not fan the flames, but I will watch it roast.

WitchIsolationResolution.5.full: {0} gains 1 {icon:Creepy_Icon} and 2 Knowledge of their choice.

WitchTensionResolution.3.short: The townsfolk feel kinship with my family's suffering, as they should. My parent's death festers within me, and I feel no pride in this place.

TenseEventBad2.2.full: I have peered into the darkness and seen the blackness of men's souls. They shamble forward in my dreams, like fresh corpses wreathed in a haze of putrefaction. Their cold hands clutch at my nightgown. When they have surrounded me fully with their numbers, filling my vision with a wall of decaying flesh - that is when I awake again, screaming.
TenseEventBad2.2.easy: I have looked into the darkness and seen how black the souls of men are. In my dreams, they walk slowly towards me, like fresh dead bodies in a cloud of rot. Their cold hands grab my nightgown. When there are so many of them around me that all I can see is a wall of rotting flesh, that is when I wake up again, screaming.
TenseEventBad2.2.short: I have seen the blackness of men's souls. In my dreams they shamble toward me like rotting corpses, clutching at my nightgown, until I wake screaming.

TenseEventBad2.3.full: These recurring dreams only amplify the anxiety I feel when I peer out my window and observe the icy gray village I once loved. Their betrayal has left me in desolate isolation, deprived of access to the resources I require. If only they could see the worth in my experiments. If only they knew how much I wallow in anguish for their sake!
TenseEventBad2.3.easy: These dreams that keep coming back make me even more nervous when I look out of my window at the cold gray village that I once loved. They betrayed me and left me completely alone, without the things I need. If only they could see the value of my experiments. If only they knew how much I suffer for them!
TenseEventBad2.3.short: These dreams deepen my dread as I look out at the icy village I once loved. Their betrayal has cut me off from what I need. If only they saw the worth of my experiments, and how I suffer for them!

TenseEventBad2.4.full: They have already pushed me this far, why should I be denied the resources for which I am so desperate? Even if I must retrieve them through more venomous means, I am firm in my convictions. But I will need the help of my cousins to complete this task. I plan to write them on the morrow!
TenseEventBad2.4.easy: They have already pushed me this far. Why should I not get the things I need so badly? Even if I must get them in more poisonous ways, I am sure of what I believe. But I will need my cousins' help for this task. I plan to write to them tomorrow!
TenseEventBad2.4.short: Why should I be denied what I so desperately need? I will get it, by venomous means if I must, but I need my cousins' help. I will write to them tomorrow!

Guilt.3.full: The experiment is complete, but I cannot bear to look upon it! What foul work! I have remained in my bedchamber for weeks in a wretched state of remorse. But, when I emerge from my infernal cocoon of solitude, I will rip that cursed page from my journal and throw it hence into the fireplace.
Guilt.3.easy: The experiment is finished, but I cannot look at it! What horrible work! I have stayed in my bedroom for weeks, feeling terrible and sorry. But when I come out of my dark, lonely shell, I will tear that cursed page out of my journal and throw it into the fire.
Guilt.3.short: The experiment is complete, but I cannot bear to look at it! I have hidden in my bedchamber for weeks, consumed by remorse. When I emerge, I will tear that cursed page from my journal and burn it.

Though I am sure these dim souls haven't quite determined what that means exactly, they are raising funds for the vague plans of a memorial.

I am sure these simple people do not really know what that means, but they are collecting money for some unclear plans for a memorial.
CommemorativeIntro.4.short: Despite the gloom, a growing movement wants stability and to celebrate what makes {0} unique. Though unsure what that means, they are raising funds for a memorial.

CommemorativeIntro.5.full: Doomed to failure, most likely. However, if having my initials inscribed onto a brick could somehow chase away the rabble from my doorstep, I may reluctantly oblige.
CommemorativeIntro.5.easy: It will probably fail. But if having my initials written on a brick could somehow keep the crowd away from my door, I might agree to it, even if I do not want to.
CommemorativeIntro.5.short: Doomed, most likely. But if my initials on a brick keep the rabble from my door, I may oblige.

FPResearch2signin.3.easy: Yesterday evening, a local noble and inventor received the first yearly prize for science, for their excellent work. The prize was given at a ceremony on their newly repaired land, which looks down on the village of {0}.
FPResearch2signin.3.short: Last night a local aristocrat and inventor received the first annual science award, at a ceremony on their renovated grounds above {0}.

FPResearch2signin.4.full: Upon accepting the award from the University of Iaşi, the fellow made these remarks: "I want to advance Science at all costs. No mountain is too high. No religious or ethical boundary too compelling. My important work will usher in a new age - the Age of SCIENCE!"
FPResearch2signin.4.easy: When they accepted the prize from the University of Iaşi, the inventor said: "I want to move Science forward, whatever it costs. No mountain is too high. No limit of religion or right and wrong can stop me. My important work will start a new age: the Age of SCIENCE!"
FPResearch2signin.4.short: Accepting the award from the University of Iaşi, they declared: "I will advance Science at all costs. No religious or ethical boundary will stop me. My work will usher in the Age of SCIENCE!"

FPSanity3signin.3.full: The level of paranoia I have witnessed among the townsfolk would be unfathomable if I had not seen it with my own eyes. I believe - as an anonymous and unbiased person without any scientific background - it is of utmost importance for us to push past these ridiculous preconceptions and expand our acceptance of new ideas.
FPSanity3signin.3.easy: I could not believe how much fear there is among the townspeople if I had not seen it with my own eyes. I am an unknown and fair person without any scientific training, and I believe it is very important for us to move past these silly old ideas and to be more open to new ideas.
FPSanity3signin.3.short: I would not believe the townsfolk's paranoia had I not seen it. As an anonymous, unbiased layperson, I believe we must move past these ridiculous prejudices and embrace new ideas.

FPSanity3signin.4.full: Who are we to judge a person for returning to the same shop several times in a week to purchase a live rabbit? Or to peruse the caravans for curiosities and trinkets? Who among us has not spent several dark evenings contemplating their existence among the graves in the cemetery?
FPSanity3signin.4.easy: Who are we to judge a person who goes back to the same shop several times a week to buy a live rabbit? Or who looks through the caravans for strange things and small treasures? Which of us has not spent several dark evenings among the graves in the cemetery, thinking about life?
FPSanity3signin.4.short: Who are we to judge someone for buying live rabbits several times a week, browsing the caravans for curiosities, or brooding among the graves at night?

FPSanity3signin.5.full: A person should be judged by their results, not by the means by which they achieve them.
FPSanity3signin.5.easy: We should judge a person by their results, not by how they get them.

FPCreepy3signin.3.full: ...I decided to ask about more pressing matters and several behavior complaints logged by citizens at the local town hall. However, as I was about to make my inquiry, a black carriage rode by and both passenger and driver alike made stern looks in our direction.
FPCreepy3signin.3.easy: ...I decided to ask about more important things, like several complaints about bad behavior that citizens had written down at the local town hall. But just as I was about to ask, a black carriage drove past, and both the passenger and the driver looked at us very seriously.
FPCreepy3signin.3.short: ...I turned to more pressing matters: complaints filed at the town hall about their behavior. But as I began, a black carriage passed, its passenger and driver glaring at us.

FPCreepy3signin.4.full: It appeared this treatment was enough for my companion to throw down their handkerchief and look towards the sky with menace. "How dare they turn their sullen glances towards me! I'll show them. I'll show them all!" The regal entrepreneur then let out a hearty laugh which both confused and delighted passersby. I decided to assume this was a cue to postpone any further interview when the laughter continued for several minutes unabated.
FPCreepy3signin.4.easy: It seems this was enough to make my companion throw down their handkerchief and look up at the sky with an angry face. "How dare they look at me so darkly! I'll show them. I'll show them all!" Then the noble business person laughed loudly, which confused and pleased the people walking by. The laughing went on for several minutes without stopping, so I decided that it was time to end the interview for now.
FPCreepy3signin.4.short: This was enough for my companion to throw down their handkerchief and glare at the sky. "How dare they! I'll show them all!" They then laughed heartily for several minutes, and I took it as a cue to end the interview.

FPNo.3.full: Even having already determined my fate, I was still unable to control my ambitious impulses. Curse my own ceaseless ambition!
FPNo.3.easy: I had already decided my future, but I still could not control my wish to achieve great things. Curse my ambition that never stops!

FPNo.4.full: Today, the townspeople whispered as I walked by. They distrust the science I am perfecting. They make casual accusations of vile acts which I could not repeat in writing. I have resigned myself to retreating to my estate for now. Away from the prying eyes and chattering gossip of the peasantry.
FPNo.4.easy: Today, the townspeople whispered as I walked past. They do not trust the science I am making perfect. They carelessly accuse me of horrible things that I cannot write down. I have accepted that I must go back to my house for now, away from the curious eyes and the gossip of the farmers.
FPNo.4.short: Today the townspeople whispered as I passed, distrusting my science and accusing me of vile acts. For now I retreat to my estate, away from their prying eyes.

FPNo.5.full: **Immediately gain 1 {icon:Creepy_Icon}.** The token remains where it is, until another player claims it.

ManiaSpecial.4.full: The cold and dark landscape should by all accounts be an affront to my demeanor - and it certainly is to my spouse - but I find myself rejuvenated in a way that beguiles my rational mind. They say that ashes can enrich the soil and make the next harvest stronger. Well, if the grayness of this countryside serves as an ample fertilizer, my mind is a germinating seed ready to burst from the Earth.
ManiaSpecial.4.easy: The cold and dark country should make me unhappy, and it certainly makes my spouse unhappy. But I feel full of new energy, in a way that confuses my logical mind. People say that ashes make the soil richer and the next harvest stronger. Well, if the grayness of this country is good fertilizer, my mind is a seed that is ready to break out of the earth.
ManiaSpecial.4.short: This cold, dark land should depress me, and it does my spouse, yet I feel strangely rejuvenated. If ashes enrich the soil, this gray countryside has made my mind a seed ready to burst forth.

ManiaSpecial.5.full: This collective mania - it is contagious. Each day I find my mind wandering, dreaming up new formulas and calculations, drafting notes as if possessed by some unseen force. For now, I will let my thoughts go wherever they are wont to go.
ManiaSpecial.5.easy: This madness of everyone, it spreads like a disease. Every day my mind wanders. I dream of new formulas and calculations, and I write notes as if some force that I cannot see controls me. For now, I will let my thoughts go wherever they want.
ManiaSpecial.5.short: This collective mania is contagious. My mind wanders to new formulas, as if possessed. For now, I let it.

ManiaSpecial.6.full: However, I will find my true calling. In this frenzied era of wild ideas and incendiary superstitions, I will emerge focused and determined!
ManiaSpecial.6.easy: But I will find my true purpose. In this wild time of crazy ideas and dangerous superstitions, I will come out of it focused and determined!

FP10VPsignin.3.full: A local entrepreneur and inventor has recently caught the eye of the populace, for better or worse. While their experimentations have become public due to their loud and extravagant nature, this ambition has caused old questions to resurface as to the family's legacy in the region.
FP10VPsignin.3.easy: A local business person and inventor has recently been noticed by the people, for better or for worse. Their experiments have become well known because they are so loud and showy, and this ambition has made people ask old questions again about the family's history in the region.
FP10VPsignin.3.short: A local entrepreneur and inventor has caught the public eye. Their loud, extravagant experiments have revived old questions about the family's legacy.

FP10VPsignin.4.full: The entrepreneurs' spirit has been on record at several occasions in recent history. "I want fame and fortune," the aristocrat proclaimed without prompting. "So I will have it. Then he raised his black cloak up to just below his eyes and left my house quickly but elegantly, with his men behind him. How rude of that person to suggest such a thing! I cannot understand why they did not contact the person who handles the inheritance to solve their small money problems!
Payment1NoC.3.short: "Our employer will not be pleased," the other hissed, raising his ebony cloak and sweeping out with his followers. The nerve! Why not take such minor quibbles to the executor?

Payment1NoD.3.short: "Our employer will not be pleased," the other hissed, raising his ebony cloak and sweeping out with his followers. The nerve! Why not take such minor quibbles to the executor?

Payment1ThanksC.3.full: The men were pleased with my generous decision and pledged to never return again. Though they expressed themselves firmly, I was impressed to see them turn and gracefully exit without leaving a single speck of dust upon the carpeted entryway.
Payment1ThanksC.3.easy: The men were happy with my generous decision and promised never to come back. They spoke firmly, but I was impressed that they turned and left elegantly, without leaving one bit of dust on the carpet at the entrance.
Payment1ThanksC.3.short: Pleased with my generosity, the men promised never to return, and left gracefully without a speck of dust on the carpet.

Payment1ThanksD.3.full: The men were pleased with my generous decision and pledged to never return again. Though they expressed themselves firmly, I was impressed to see them turn and gracefully exit without leaving a single speck of dust upon the carpeted entryway.
Payment1ThanksD.3.easy: The men were happy with my generous decision and promised never to come back. They spoke firmly, but I was impressed that they turned and left elegantly, without leaving one bit of dust on the carpet at the entrance.
Payment1ThanksD.3.short: Pleased with my generosity, the men promised never to return, and left gracefully without a speck of dust on the carpet.

JailEvent1.3.full: I met with their leader just days previous, through coercive means I assure you. There I was, forced to mingle with criminals and rust-covered sociopaths in coveralls, bruised and thrust upon the steps of the prison, or what they now call the Junk Palace.
JailEvent1.3.easy: I met their leader just a few days ago, and I promise you, they forced me to come. I had to be among criminals and dangerous people in dirty work clothes covered in rust. I was hurt and pushed onto the steps of the prison, or what they now call the Junk Palace.
JailEvent1.3.short: Days ago I was forced to meet their leader, shoved bruised among criminals onto the steps of the prison, now called the Junk Palace.

JailEvent1.4.full: A man stepped forward to the cheers of a throng of miscreants. The man was strong and rough with a ruddy complexion, a broad, square jaw, and a beard separated by deep scars along his cheeks. He wore a thick apron with one shoulder strap ripped at the seams. The front was covered in dark stains, and by his confident stride, he seemed to revel in its uncleanliness. In his gloved hand, he held a hammer which dripped with a red substance that also stained his fingers.
JailEvent1.4.easy: A man stepped forward while a crowd of criminals cheered. The man was strong and rough, with a red face, a wide square jaw, and a beard cut through by deep scars on his cheeks. He wore a thick apron, and one of its shoulder straps was torn. The front was covered in dark stains, and from the proud way he walked, he seemed to enjoy how dirty it was. In his gloved hand, he held a hammer that dripped with something red, which was also on his fingers.
JailEvent1.4.short: To cheers from the miscreants, a man stepped forward: strong, ruddy, square-jawed, his beard split by scars. His stained apron hung from one torn strap, and his gloved hand held a hammer dripping red.

JailEvent1.5.full: A woman stepped forward to the cheers of a throng of miscreants. Her hair was cropped shorter than a bob, dark and wild with a sheen of oil. It framed her angular face and draped over a black eye-patch that covered her left eye. She wore a thick apron that was once white, but now stained a dark crimson with fresh droplets of red bespattered across the chest. In her gloved hand, she held a metal cleaver, rusted near the handle, with thick divots in the blade from years of use.
JailEvent1.5.easy: A woman stepped forward while a crowd of criminals cheered. Her hair was cut very short, dark and wild, and shiny with oil. It was around her sharp face and fell over a black eye patch on her left eye. She wore a thick apron that was once white, but was now dark red, with fresh red drops on the chest. In her gloved hand, she held a metal butcher's knife. It was rusty near the handle, and the blade had deep marks from years of use.
JailEvent1.5.short: To cheers from the miscreants, a woman stepped forward: wild, oily, cropped hair, a black patch over her left eye, a once-white apron now crimson. Her gloved hand held a rusted, notched cleaver.

JailEvent1.6.full: "They call me {0}. Perhaps you remember my family, and how they were ruined by the accusations of hysterical peons so many generations ago. Well now, us unfortunate wretches have taken back what is rightfully ours. {1} runs this town."
JailEvent1.6.easy: "They call me {0}. Maybe you remember my family, and how they were destroyed by the accusations of crazy, unimportant people so many generations ago. Well, now we poor people have taken back what belongs to us. {1} runs this town."
JailEvent1.6.short: "They call me {0}. Perhaps you remember how my family was ruined by hysterical accusations generations ago. Now we wretches have taken back what is ours. {1} runs this town."

JailEvent1.7.full: The aberrant horde roared their approval. The malcontented rabble beat their chests and clattered metal upon metal.
JailEvent1.7.easy: The strange crowd roared that they agreed. The unhappy people beat their chests and hit metal against metal.

JailEvent1.8.full: I spied a shadowy figure within the Junk Palace, its distorted silhouette framed against the entryway for a moment before disappearing once again. Was this the same creature I had hunted for?
JailEvent1.8.easy: I saw a dark shape inside the Junk Palace. Its twisted outline stood in the entrance for a moment, and then it disappeared again. Was this the same creature I had hunted?
JailEvent1.8.short: A distorted silhouette appeared in the Junk Palace doorway, then vanished. Was it the creature I had hunted?

JailEvent1.9.full: "I have brought you here because you are useful. But mark my words, {0} expects loyalty."
JailEvent1.9.easy: "I have brought you here because you are useful. But remember what I say: {0} expects loyalty."

JailEvent1A.3.full: While I despised this cretin for their signature treatment of me, I also felt a strange sense of pride that my experiments had been appreciated, even by one so base. {0} commanded an authority that I could not help but admire when the fear of immediate death had left me.
JailEvent1A.3.easy: I hated this stupid person for the way they treated me. But I also felt strangely proud that my experiments were respected, even by someone so low. When I was no longer afraid of dying at once, I could not stop admiring how much authority {0} had.
JailEvent1A.3.short: I despised this cretin's treatment of me, yet felt proud that even they valued my experiments. Once I no longer feared instant death, I could not help admiring {0}'s authority.

JailEvent1A.4.full: "You will **build a warrior** to fight in the arena as will the rest of your kin. The winner will escape with their life. The rusted losers will be ground to dust for all to see on the floor of the Battledome. {0} has spoken and so it will be done!"
JailEvent1A.4.easy: "You will **build a warrior** to fight in the arena, and so will the rest of your family. The winner will escape with their life. The rusty losers will be crushed to dust on the floor of the Battledome, for everyone to see. {0} has spoken, and so it will be done!"
JailEvent1A.4.short: "You and your kin will each **build a warrior** for the arena. The winner lives. The losers will be ground to dust on the Battledome floor. {0} has spoken!"

JailEvent1A.5.full: Retrieve the cross-shaped **Battledome Warrior** tiles and give one to each player.

JailEvent1A.6.full: At the End of the Generation, each player will choose their single best Experiment of each type, place it face up in each of the 4 slots, and add its strength (VP total) to assemble their **Warrior** as noted on the Battledome Warrior tiles.

ENTERTHEBATTLEDOME.2.full: The exterior of the iron dome was decorated extensively for the event, with sanguine cloths weaved into the archway at the front gate and a wild jumble of interconnected copper pipes sibilating with pressurized steam. With a loud whistle, the grand aluminium doors pistoned open, revealing the cracked earth of an ovular arena. All around myself and my cousins, the deranged citizens cheered in their strange attire and distorted physiques; begoggled and covered in an imposing mishmash of rusted metal and leather.
ENTERTHEBATTLEDOME.2.easy: The outside of the iron dome was decorated a lot for the event. There were blood-red cloths woven into the arch at the front gate, and a wild mess of connected copper pipes hissed with steam. With a loud whistle, the big aluminium doors opened like machines and showed the cracked ground of an oval arena. All around me and my cousins, the crazy citizens cheered. They wore strange clothes, and their bodies were twisted. They had goggles and were covered in a frightening mix of rusty metal and leather.
ENTERTHEBATTLEDOME.2.short: The iron dome was decked in blood-red cloth and hissing copper pipes. With a whistle, the great doors opened onto a cracked oval arena, and around us the deranged citizens cheered in goggles, rusted metal and leather.

ENTERTHEBATTLEDOME.3.full: {0} sat on a copper throne at one end, its extensive base crafted from metal scraps.
ENTERTHEBATTLEDOME.3.easy: {0} sat on a copper throne at one end. Its large base was made from pieces of scrap metal.

ENTERTHEBATTLEDOME.4.full: My cousins and I had completed all other tasks. There was only this one final obligation. Before I left this world, I would cover this arena with blood and oil. The battle was on!
ENTERTHEBATTLEDOME.4.easy: My cousins and I had finished all our other tasks. There was only this one last duty. Before I left this world, I would cover this arena with blood and oil. The battle had begun!
ENTERTHEBATTLEDOME.4.short: All other tasks were done. One duty remained: to cover this arena in blood and oil. The battle was on!

AsylumTreatment.2.easy: *An old page lists when visitors came into the Asylum and when they left. The list also shows the names of people who came in to have their minds examined.*

Prologue-FOTU.3.full: I have made much progress in my research over these last months. My host has furnished me with appropriate accommodations and the food is hearty with a warmth that lifts the spirits. While I am gracious for their hospitality, I have yet to give my appreciation in person. The caretaker assures me that they are on extended holiday, but their absence is peculiar. Something about this arrangement unnerves me, though I cannot for the life of me determine its source.
Prologue-FOTU.3.easy: I have made a lot of progress in my research over the last months. My host has given me good rooms, and the food is rich and warm and makes me feel happy. I am thankful for their kindness, but I have not yet been able to thank them in person. The caretaker says that they are on a long holiday, but it is strange that they are not here. Something about this situation makes me nervous, but I really cannot say why.
Prologue-FOTU.3.short: My research has progressed well. My host has provided fine rooms and hearty food, though I have yet to meet them; the caretaker says they are on extended holiday. Their absence unnerves me, though I cannot say why.

Prologue-FOTU.4.full: It is but a minor xenophobia, a fear of the unknown that sets my eyes to dwelling on the dark corners of this unfamiliar, decaying, but immaculate estate. At night, I perceive to hear the echoes of a distant hammering, the scraping of metal on metal, the rumble of thunder. Yet when I sash my nightgown tight and emerge upon the veranda, the misty countryside is spread wide under the moon and I am greeted with nothing but the echo of cicadas and the smell of tulips in the night air.
Prologue-FOTU.4.easy: It is only a small fear of the strange, a fear of the unknown, that makes me look into the dark corners of this unfamiliar, old, but very clean house. At night, I think I hear the sound of hammering far away, metal scraping on metal, and thunder. But when I tie my nightgown tight and go out onto the veranda, I see the foggy country under the moon, and there is nothing but the sound of insects and the smell of tulips in the night air.
Prologue-FOTU.4.short: A fear of the unknown makes me dwell on the dark corners of this decaying, immaculate estate. At night I seem to hear distant hammering and scraping metal. Yet on the veranda there is only moonlit mist, cicadas and the scent of tulips.

Prologue-FOTU.5.full: The business at hand: Included within the accompanying package is an extensive collection of clippings, journal entries, and letters chronicling the storied history of this peculiar estate and its proprietors. Their contents are fascinating and I have arranged them in a semblance of order which tells a vivid, extraordinary tale.
Prologue-FOTU.5.easy: Now to business: In the package with this letter, you will find a large collection of newspaper articles, journal pages, and letters. They tell the long history of this strange house and its owners. What they say is fascinating, and I have put them in an order that tells a clear and extraordinary story.
Prologue-FOTU.5.short: The business at hand: the enclosed package holds clippings, journals and letters chronicling this estate and its owners. I have ordered them into an extraordinary tale.

Prologue-FOTU.6.full: I expect to return to London shortly, but I have posted this ahead of my arrival so as to make the burden lighter for me. I fear I don't have the same fortitude that I once did. If perchance something were to happen to me, I trust you will ensure its publication in whatever form you see fit.
Prologue-FOTU.6.easy: I expect to go back to London soon, but I have sent this before I arrive, so that I have less to carry. I am afraid I am not as strong as I once was. If something should happen to me, I trust you to publish it in whatever way you think is best.
Prologue-FOTU.6.short: I will return to London soon, but have sent this ahead. I am not as strong as I was. Should anything happen to me, please publish it as you see fit.

Prologue-FOTU.7.full: As always, I think of you fondly. Give mother my warmest regards.
Prologue-FOTU.7.easy: As always, I think of you with love. Please give mother my warmest wishes.

RevengePlot35.2.full: **Carefully pick up this Storybook device and hand it to the player with the least VP.** *If there is a tie, hand this to the one who was last in turn order in the previous round.* **Do not allow any other players to see the screen.**

RevengePlot35.4.full: Perhaps it was fate that understood my current misfortune and lackluster position compared to my cousins. But, a messenger arrived one day with an offer of punishment or deliverance that I alone would comprehend.
RevengePlot35.4.easy: Maybe it was fate, which understood my bad luck and how weak my position was compared to my cousins. One day, a messenger came with an offer of punishment or rescue that only I would understand.
RevengePlot35.4.short: Perhaps fate saw my misfortune beside my cousins. One day a messenger came with an offer of punishment or deliverance that only I would understand.

RevengePlot35.6.full: A {icon:StorybookToken} token will be placed on the **35VP** space of the VP Track. When the first player reaches this VP amount (including yourself), either fortune or misfortune will befall them.

RevengePlot35.8.full: - The player will move forward one space for free on any Journal Track.

RevengePlot35.11.full: - The player will lose 3VP and send a Servant to Lost.

RevengePlotFortune.1.full: **Do not read the passage below to the other players.**

RevengePlotFortune.3.full: I, of course, chose **Fortune.** I was supremely confident in my abilities and in the utter ineptitude of my competition that I would claim this fortune before they would be able.
RevengePlotFortune.3.easy: Of course, I chose **Fortune.** I was completely sure of my abilities, and sure that my rivals were so useless that I would get this fortune before they could.
RevengePlotFortune.3.short: I chose **Fortune**, of course, certain I would claim it before my inept competition could.

RevengePlotFortune.4.full: Place a **{icon:StorybookToken} token** on the **35** space of the VP Track.

RevengePlotMisfortune.1.full: **Do not read the passage below to the other players.**

RevengePlotMisfortune.3.full: I, of course, chose **Misfortune.** Let this one act be the catalyst that dooms them to hell for their treacherous ways. May a thousand other miseries torment their souls. For I wish far greater ill upon them that hold me in such low regard!
RevengePlotMisfortune.3.easy: Of course, I chose **Misfortune.** Let this one action be what sends them to hell for their betrayal. May a thousand other sorrows hurt their souls. Because I wish much worse things on the people who think so little of me!
RevengePlotMisfortune.3.short: I chose **Misfortune**, of course. Let it doom them to hell for their treachery, and may a thousand miseries follow!

RevengePlotMisfortune.4.full: Place a **{icon:StorybookToken} token** on the **35** space of the VP Track.

35Fortune.4.full: A curious thing happened this morning. A courier arrived at my doorstep unannounced with a package. Upon opening it, I discovered a variety of notes and papers detailing unpublished scientific theories the likes of which caused my heart to quicken its pace. They appeared to be speckled with dried blood from an unknown source, but otherwise perfectly legible.
35Fortune.4.easy: A strange thing happened this morning. A messenger came to my door without warning, with a package. When I opened it, I found many notes and papers about scientific ideas that had never been published, and they made my heart beat faster. There were small spots of dried blood on them, from who knows where, but I could read them perfectly.
35Fortune.4.short: This morning a courier brought an unexpected package: unpublished scientific theories that set my heart racing. Speckled with dried blood, but perfectly legible.

35Fortune.5.full: No matter. What a marvelous boon!

35Fortune.6.full: Immediately **move forward one space on any Journal Track** for no Knowledge cost. Then, return the {icon:StorybookToken} token to the supply.

35Misfortune.4.full: Today, I awoke to the unfortunate news that one of my servants had been burned alive while tending to the laundry. While certainly my recent laboratory security improvements may have been the culprit, the spontaneous combustion of human beings is still a rarity.
35Misfortune.4.easy: Today, I woke up to the sad news that one of my servants had burned to death while washing the clothes. It is possible that my recent safety changes in the laboratory were the cause, but it is still very rare for people to suddenly catch fire by themselves.
35Misfortune.4.short: Today a servant burned alive doing the laundry. My new laboratory security may be to blame, but spontaneous human combustion is still rare.

35Misfortune.5.full: Suspect foul play. Will return to this after tea. Be sure to collect ashes.

35Misfortune.6.full: Immediately **lose 3VP** and **return one of your Servants to Lost**. Then, return the {icon:StorybookToken} token to the supply.

Creepy1stPlayer.4.full: It is deplorable in the highest degree for the people to distrust our presence because of the detestable business of our progenitors. {0} is the place of my birth! Yet, here I write to you in haste with a fire to my diction. These cretins would penalize us for our very existence! They eye us with such apprehension that it preys upon my anxieties at every stretch.
Creepy1stPlayer.4.easy: It is terrible that people do not trust us because of the horrible business of our ancestors. {0} is where I was born! But here I am, writing to you quickly and angrily. These stupid people want to punish us just for being alive! They look at us with so much fear that it makes me nervous everywhere I go.
Creepy1stPlayer.4.short: It is deplorable that people distrust us for our ancestors' deeds. {0} is my birthplace! These cretins would punish us for existing, and their wary stares gnaw at my nerves.

Creepy1stPlayer.5.full: A pox on their wild superstitions! Oh, how I wish I were back in university!
Creepy1stPlayer.5.easy: Curse their wild superstitions! Oh, how I wish I were back at university!

Creepy1stPlayer.6.full: The player(s) with the most VP immediately **gains 2 {icon:Creepy_Icon}.**

Creepy1stPlayerB.3.full: The burden of fame has finally pressed its weight upon me. It is obvious from the awestruck silence upon my visits, that my cousins view me as an unrivaled inspiration and this sentiment has seeped into the mindset of the burghers as well.
Creepy1stPlayerB.3.easy: Being famous has finally become a heavy weight for me. When I visit, everyone is silent with wonder. It is clear that my cousins see me as an inspiration that nobody can match, and the townspeople have started to think the same.
Creepy1stPlayerB.3.short: Fame weighs on me at last. My visits are met with awed silence; my cousins see me as an unrivaled inspiration, and so do the burghers.

Creepy1stPlayerB.4.full: While it vexes me to lose time to matters of local import, I cannot fault them for their inquiries. With the paranoiae of the past fading and my exemplary leadership on display, it is only natural. My affluence is my curse.
Creepy1stPlayerB.4.easy: It annoys me to lose time with local matters, but I cannot blame them for asking. The fears of the past are going away, and everyone can see what an excellent leader I am, so it is only natural. Being rich is my curse.
Creepy1stPlayerB.4.short: Local matters waste my time, but with the old paranoia fading and my leadership on display, it is only natural. My affluence is my curse.

Creepy1stPlayerB.5.full: What a bother it is to be so popular.
Creepy1stPlayerB.5.easy: What a nuisance it is to be so popular.

Creepy1stPlayerB.6.full: The player(s) with the most VP immediately **loses 1 {icon:Creepy_Icon}** and **discards 1 Experiment card** during the Start of a Generation phase.

PrivateCountYesNo.2.full: The Count returned this afternoon to make good on his promise of investment opportunities to our family. I noted how strange it was that my brief recollections of him as a child proved to be spot on. While my parents had passed, the Count seemed to have never aged a single day. The benefits of a healthy disposition and good living, I suppose.
PrivateCountYesNo.2.easy: The Count came back this afternoon to keep his promise of business opportunities for our family. I noticed how strange it was that my short memories of him from when I was a child were exactly right. My parents had died, but the Count did not seem to have become one day older. That is what a healthy life and good living do, I suppose.
PrivateCountYesNo.2.short: The Count returned today to offer our family the promised investments. Strangely, he looked exactly as I remembered from childhood. My parents are gone, yet he has not aged a day. Good living, I suppose.

PrivateCountYesNo.3.full: Each player **gains a Servant** from Lost.

CreaturePleased.2.full: An uncanny occurrence today: I was skimming through my family's notes and found references to an experiment to procure life from death. At this same moment, I received a letter with very poor penmanship from an individual signed only as **The Creature.**
CreaturePleased.2.easy: A strange thing happened today: I was looking through my family's notes and found mentions of an experiment to make life from death. At the same moment, I got a letter with very bad handwriting from someone who only signed as **The Creature.**
CreaturePleased.2.short: Uncanny: just as I found notes on my family's experiment to create life from death, a badly written letter arrived, signed only **The Creature.**

CreaturePleased.3.full: The letter reads: "I wish to alleviate some of what ails you. Even from the cold of Siberia, where I reside away from the wretched eyes of humanity, I hear word of {0} and its troubles.
CreaturePleased.3.easy: The letter says: "I want to make some of your problems smaller. Even from cold Siberia, where I live far away from the terrible eyes of people, I hear news of {0} and its troubles.

CreaturePleased.4.full: I offer you this remuneration with no obligation. Your family may have cursed me, but it has also soothed the rage within me."
CreaturePleased.4.easy: I give you this payment and you owe me nothing. Your family may have cursed me, but it has also calmed the anger inside me."

CreaturePleased.5.full: All players' remaining debts to **the Count** are removed.

PlotPlayerCheckin.4.full: Last evening they congregated outside my gates, pitchforks and torches raised with aims to forcefully remove me from my own home. Had I not released the hounds to snap and gnaw at their efforts, their attempt may have been successful. Oh, why do they despise me so?
PlotPlayerCheckin.4.easy: Last evening they gathered outside my gates with pitchforks and torches, ready to throw me out of my own home by force. If I had not let the dogs out to bite at them, they might have succeeded. Oh, why do they hate me so much?
PlotPlayerCheckin.4.short: Last night they gathered at my gates with pitchforks and torches to drive me from my home. Only the hounds stopped them. Why do they despise me so?

GainFamilyPlot.3.full: You have seen how they stare; how they accuse me without evidence or precedent. Well, I have tolerated their angry mobs and frontier justice for far too long!
GainFamilyPlot.3.easy: You have seen how they stare at me, how they accuse me without proof or reason. Well, I have accepted their angry crowds and their punishments without courts for far too long!
GainFamilyPlot.3.short: You have seen their stares and baseless accusations. I have tolerated their mobs and frontier justice for far too long!

GainFamilyPlot.5.full: **At the End of the Generation, you will gain the Family Plot Upgrade.**
