Gen3Token2.5.full: I had come to a crossroads - a self-reckoning where the distress of existence was laid bare before me. I could continue onward on my path towards my appointed Obsession or I could forge a new path, one galvanized by my own impulses - wild and unfettered. Whichever I chose, I knew then that I would need to see it through to the bitter end.
Gen3Token2.5.easy: I had come to a crossroads: a moment where I had to face myself, and where all the pain of being alive was open in front of me. I could continue on the path towards my chosen Obsession, or I could make a new path, driven by my own wishes, wild and free. Whatever I chose, I knew then that I would have to continue to the bitter end.
Gen3Token2.5.short: I had reached a crossroads. I could continue towards my appointed Obsession, or forge a new path driven by my own wild impulses. Either way, I would see it through to the bitter end.

Gen3Token2b.4.easy: Yes. For too long I have been chained to a future that was already decided, because I felt it was my duty. And for what? For ancestors who started these horrible events and forced me to live at the edge of society?
Gen3Token2b.4.short: Yes. Too long have I been chained to fate by duty, for ancestors who doomed me to life on society's fringes.

Gen3Token2b.5.full: My mind is made up. {0} I will not be tethered to the past!
Gen3Token2b.5.easy: I have decided. {0} I will not be tied to the past!

JailEventA.2.full: If this letter reaches you, I urge you to delay any potential visit to this cursed village indefinitely! The lunatics have taken over the Asylum, quite literally.
JailEventA.2.easy: If this letter reaches you, I beg you to wait with any visit to this cursed village, for as long as possible! The mad people have taken over the Asylum, really.

JailEventA.3.full: Chaos! Utter chaos is the only way to describe the ensuing rebellion which has driven out the residents of {0} and left a distorted landscape tattered in its wake. The inmates, sickened by their squalid conditions and driven deeper into madness, have reclaimed this bucolic village and transformed it into their own rusted wasteland. Oh my reckless ambitions! I have doomed this land to an apocalyptic fate.
JailEventA.3.easy: Chaos! Complete chaos is the only way to describe the rebellion that followed. It has driven the people of {0} away and left a twisted, torn land behind. The prisoners, sick of their dirty conditions and pushed deeper into madness, have taken back this pretty country village and turned it into their own rusty wasteland. Oh, my careless ambitions! I have doomed this land to the end of the world.
JailEventA.3.short: Chaos! The rebellion has driven out the people of {0}. The inmates, maddened by squalor, have turned the village into a rusted wasteland. My reckless ambitions have doomed this land!

JailEventA.4.full: Even now, the rivers run red with blood and acid mine drainage. How wrong I was to assume this exploitative business would be the end of things! Am I cursed to forever suffer for my family's hubris?
JailEventA.4.easy: Even now, the rivers are red with blood and poisonous water from the mines. How wrong I was to think that this greedy business would be the end of it! Must I suffer forever for my family's pride?
JailEventA.4.short: The rivers run red with blood and mine drainage. Am I cursed to suffer forever for my family's hubris?

The iron grate on the opening had been torn from the concrete and left mangled and exposed to the elements. It cast a twisted shadow across the stone floor. "I see that you are a monster by nature. And one cannot be blamed for simply following one's natural impulses."
PrivateReward1.3.easy: "What a joy it is to see your soul so openly," {0} said to me, while looking out of a window in the broken dining hall. PrivateReward1.8.full: It was then that I was offered a choice that I did not expect and pondered on my carriage ride home. This patronizing generosity vexed me, but the words echoed in my mind.

PaymentOrDeathB.5.full: I do not know how they got past my defenses, but these pale individuals dressed in angular, coal-black suits came to my door seeking payment of an old debt. When my caretaker forbade them entry, they merely separated the double-door from its hinges without the use of weapons. Even now they skulk about, calling me by name and hissing like an alleycat protecting its meal.
PaymentOrDeathB.5.easy: I do not know how they got past my defenses, but these pale people in sharp, coal-black suits came to my door to collect an old debt. When my caretaker did not let them in, they simply took the double door off its hinges, without any weapons. Even now they move around secretly, calling my name and hissing like a street cat that protects its food.
PaymentOrDeathB.5.short: Somehow these pale figures in coal-black suits got past my defenses to collect an old debt. When my caretaker refused them, they simply lifted the doors off their hinges. Now they prowl, calling my name and hissing.

CureCountYes.3.full: The old Count smiled, assessing the schematics which I had prepared. His long fingernails carefully rolled the parchment and he wrapped it with a singular piece of twine. "This will do nicely."
CureCountYes.3.easy: The old Count smiled and looked carefully at the plans I had prepared. With his long fingernails, he carefully rolled up the paper and tied it with one piece of string. "This will do nicely."

CureCountYes.4.full: "I have made many mistakes over the past centuries. And I have made many enemies because of this. I am sorry to have misrepresented myself." The count turned towards me then, his white fangs perched upon his red lips and his elevated black collar obscuring a portion of his face. "I intend to use the cure. Just not upon myself. I will offer the cure to all of my enemies whether they crave it or not. With this, I will make these fools pay! Their bones will turn to dust, and I, Vlad Dracula will rise once more!" The old Count tilted his head back and cackled deep in his chest.
CureCountYes.4.easy: "I have made many mistakes over the last centuries. And because of this, I have made many enemies. I am sorry that I did not tell you the truth about myself." Then the count turned towards me. His white sharp teeth sat on his red lips, and his high black collar hid part of his face. "I want to use the cure. But not on myself. I will give the cure to all of my enemies, whether they want it or not. With this, I will make these fools pay! Their bones will turn to dust, and I, Vlad Dracula, will rise again!" The old Count put his head back and laughed deeply.
CureCountYes.4.short: "I have made many mistakes, and many enemies, over the centuries. Forgive my deception." He turned, fangs on red lips. "I will use the cure, not on myself, but on all my enemies, willing or not. Their bones will turn to dust, and I, Vlad Dracula, will rise once more!" He threw back his head and cackled.

CureCountYes.5.full: The Count's laughter was infectious; I could not help but join in myself.
CureCountYes.5.easy: The Count's laugh was so strong that I could not stop myself from laughing too.

CureCountYes.7.full: Discard one completed C-Level Occult Experiment.

CureCountNo.3.full: The old man suddenly became animated, doffing his feeble demeanor and hissing like a feral cat. With a dramatic flourish, he whirled his cloak about him, swiftly wrapping himself in a dark cocoon. With a sudden burst of fog, the old Count vanished as a black cat jumped onto the windowsill. The cat fled through the open window and out into the night.
CureCountNo.3.easy: Suddenly the old man became full of life. He stopped acting weak and hissed like a wild cat. With a big, dramatic movement, he swung his cloak around himself and quickly wrapped himself in a dark cocoon. In a sudden cloud of fog, the old Count disappeared, and a black cat jumped onto the windowsill. The cat ran through the open window and out into the night.
CureCountNo.3.short: The old man suddenly came alive, hissing like a feral cat. He whirled his cloak around himself and vanished in a burst of fog, and a black cat leapt from the windowsill into the night.

CureCountNo.4.full: All that remained was a red rose once stuck to his lapel, now fallen to the ground where it withered and dried right before my eyes. Perhaps, I had been rash in my judgement.
CureCountNo.4.easy: All that was left was a red rose that had been on his jacket. It had fallen to the ground, where it became dry and dead right in front of my eyes. Maybe I had decided too quickly.
CureCountNo.4.short: Only the red rose from his lapel remained, withering before my eyes. Perhaps I had been rash.

CountTestResults.2.full: The patient is perfectly physically and mentally fit. I find absolutely nothing wrong with such a fine specimen of completely normal human breedstock and am utterly confused as to why they were admitted! Such sharp teeth, such glorious pallor, such divine form; why I wish all patients were so adequately equipped.
CountTestResults.2.easy: The patient is perfectly healthy in body and mind. I find absolutely nothing wrong with such a fine example of a completely normal human, and I really do not understand why they were brought here! Such sharp teeth, such a wonderfully pale face, such a beautiful body. I wish all patients were so well made.
CountTestResults.2.short: The patient is perfectly fit in body and mind; I cannot fathom why they were admitted! Such sharp teeth, such glorious pallor. I wish all patients were so well equipped.

CountTestResults.3.full: Alas, despite such a **healthy**candidate for mental reformation, I must admit that they are too instrumental in the region to be confined to such dismal environs. No, I must satiate myself, and the Asylum, with others who are afflicted *(and less important)*. Release has thereby been procured upon certain private matters being addressed. It is my hope that they will provide a suitable referral in their stead.
CountTestResults.3.easy: Sadly, even though this is such a **healthy** person for treatment of the mind, I must admit that they are too important in the region to be locked up in such a sad place. No, I must satisfy myself, and the Asylum, with other sick people *(who are less important)*. So they can leave, once certain private matters have been taken care of. I hope that they will send us someone suitable in their place.
CountTestResults.3.short: Alas, though a **healthy** candidate, they are too important in the region to confine. I must satisfy myself, and the Asylum, with others *(less important)*. Release is granted once certain private matters are settled. I hope they will refer someone suitable.

CountTestResults.5.full: Perhaps it is unprofessional to pen my disgust upon the page, but this patient is completely undesirable for admittance. Or might I say, unfit for our institute's psychological consumption. Still, it is imperative that I negotiate the matter with the to-be-released {0} as I find myself unsatiated by this meager assessment. I am sure a referral to our glorious facility will suffice. Perhaps they know of one who is afflicted by instability - perhaps one well-fed, with rosy cheeks, and warm blood flowing through their veins.
CountTestResults.5.easy: Maybe it is not professional to write my disgust on this page, but this patient is not at all welcome here. Or I could say, not good for our institute to consume, for the mind. Still, it is very important that I discuss the matter with {0}, who will soon be released, because this poor examination has not satisfied me. I am sure that sending someone to our wonderful building will be enough. Maybe they know someone who is unstable, maybe someone well fed, with rosy cheeks and warm blood in their veins.
CountTestResults.5.short: Unprofessional, perhaps, but this patient is utterly undesirable, unfit for our institute's psychological consumption. Still, I must negotiate with the soon-to-be-released {0}, for I remain unsatiated. A referral will suffice: someone unstable, well fed, rosy-cheeked, with warm blood in their veins.
